==Original Japanese==
'''八坂神社'''・'''八阪神社'''（やさかじんじゃ）は、｢八坂」を社名に持つ[[神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]。[[弥栄神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]と表記する場合もある。
素戔嗚尊（[[スサノオ]]）をdeity（[[神仏分離]]令までは[[牛頭天王]]）とする[[祇園信仰]]の神社である。
他に祇園信仰に基づく神社nameとしては、[[祇園神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]（祇園社）、[[広峯神社 (曖昧さ回避)]][[ja:広峯神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] 、[[天王神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]（天王社）、[[津島神社 (曖昧さ回避)]][[ja:津島神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]<ref>[[津島信仰]]</ref>、[[八雲神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]、[[八重垣神社 (曖昧さ回避)]][[ja:八重垣神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] 、[[須賀神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]、[[素盞嗚神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]、[[須佐神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]、[[氷川神社 (曖昧さ回避)]][[ja:氷川神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]<ref>[[氷川信仰]]</ref>などがあり、時代や資料によって用いられる。
ただし例外として[[八坂刀売神]]を祀る八坂神社も存在する。
京都市東山区の[[八坂神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]は、全国の素戔嗚尊をdeityとする神社の総本社と主張している。神仏分離令までは[[天台宗]][[比叡山]]感神院祇園社。

== Yasaka Shrines ([[:ja:弥栄神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]][[ja:弥栄神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]) == This spelling has a few more variations in pronounciation {{TOCright}}
'''弥栄神社'''、'''彌榮神社'''、彌栄神社（いやさかじんじゃ、やさかじんじゃ、やえじんじゃ、やえいじんじゃ）は、[[牛頭天王]]・[[スサノオ]]をdeityとする[[祇園信仰]]の神社。
ほかに祇園信仰に基づく神社nameとしては、[[八坂神社_(曖昧さ回避)]][[ja:八坂神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]（八阪神社）、[[祇園神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]、[[広峯神社_(曖昧さ回避)]][[ja:広峯神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]、[[天王神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]、[[八雲神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]、[[須賀神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]、[[素盞嗚神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]があり、時代や資料によって通用される。
== 主な神社 == * [[弥栄神社 (標茶町)]][[ja:弥栄神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] – [[北海道]][[標茶町]] * [[弥栄神社 (長野市)]][[ja:弥栄神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] – [[長野県]][[長野市]][[長野 (長野市)#上西之門町]] * [[弥栄神社 (みよし市)]][[ja:弥栄神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] – [[愛知県]][[みよし市]] * [[弥栄神社 (豊橋市)]][[ja:弥栄神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] – 愛知県[[みよし市]] * [[彌榮神社 (大阪市)]][[ja:彌榮神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] – [[大阪府]][[大阪市]][[生野区]][[桃谷]] ： 牛頭天王社と呼ばれた。typeは旧村社。 * [[彌榮神社 (東大阪市)]][[ja:彌榮神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] – 大阪府[[東大阪市]] ： 中小阪と宝持に二社ある（一時期合祀されていた）。 * [[弥栄神社 (岸和田市)]][[ja:弥栄神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] – 大阪府[[岸和田市]]八幡町 ： typeは旧村社。[[八坂神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]から勧請。 * [[弥栄神社 (津和野町)]][[ja:弥栄神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] – [[島根県]][[鹿足郡]][[津和野町]]後田 ： typeは旧郷社。八坂神社から勧請。 * [[弥栄神社 (大分市)]][[ja:弥栄神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] – [[大分県]][[大分市]]上野738 ： typeは旧県社

[[Category:Shrine disambiguations]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] {{citation needed|Yasaka Shrine (disambiguation)}}[[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] [[Category:Shrine disambiguations]][[de:Yasaka-Schreine]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] {{citation needed|Yasaka Shrine (disambiguation)}}[[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] [[Category:Shrine disambiguations]][[ja:八坂神社 (曖昧さ回避)]] {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|250px|right]] | name = Yasaka Shrine (八坂神社) | location = [[Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka]], [[Kitakyushu]], [[Kokurakita Ward]], {{ill|Jōnai|ja|城内 (北九州市)}} | coordinates = {{Coord|33|53|07.68|N|130|52|25.39|E|region:JP-40_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Yasaka Shrine}} | Deities = {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊}} (formerly {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王}}) | type = [[Prefectural Shrine|Ken-sha]] (as of May 15, Meiji 6) | Established = {{ill|Hosokawa Tadaoki|ja|細川忠興}}, [[Genna (era)|Genna]] 3 (1617) | Main Hall = Nagare-zukuri | Festival = [[Kokura Gion Daiko]] (third Saturday/Sunday in July) }}
'''Yasaka Shrine''' (八坂神社・八阪神社, やさかじんじゃ) refers to {{ill|Shinto shrines|ja|神社}} named "Yasaka." It is sometimes written as {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|弥栄神社}}, which is covered in another article.
These shrines are dedicated to {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊}}, the deity of {{ill|Gion faith|ja|祇園信仰}}. Before the {{ill|Shinto-Buddhism Separation Order|ja|神仏分離令}}, Susanoo-no-Mikoto was identified with {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王}}.
Other names based on Gion faith include {{ill|Gion Shrine|ja|祇園神社|lt=Gion Shrines}}, {{ill|Hiromine Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|広峯神社 (曖昧さ回避)|lt=Hiromine Shrines}}, {{ill|Tennō Shrine|ja|天王神社|lt=Tennō Shrines}}, {{ill|Tsushima Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|津島神社|lt=Tsushima Shrines}}, {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲神社|lt=Yakumo Shrines}}, {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|八重垣神社|lt=Yaegaki Shrines}}, {{ill|Suga Shrine|ja|須賀神社}}, {{ill|Susanoo Shrine|ja|素盞嗚神社}}, {{ill|Susa Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|須佐神社|Susa Shrine (disambiguation)=Susa Shrine (disambiguation)|lt=Susa Shrine}}, and {{ill|Hikawa Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|氷川神社}}.
Notably, some exceptions include Yasaka shrines that enshrine {{ill|Yasakatome-no-Kami|ja|八坂刀売神}}.
== Main Shrine == [[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|thumb|250px|right|Kyoto's {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|八坂神社}}, one of the head shrines]] * '''{{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|八坂神社}}''' ({{ill|Higashiyama Ward, Kyoto|ja|京都市東山区}}) – Formerly {{ill|Kanjin'in Gion-sha|ja|感神院祇園社}} under {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗}} and {{ill|Mount Hiei|ja|比叡山}} until the Shinto-Buddhism Separation Order. Claimed as the main shrine of Susanoo-no-Mikoto nationwide.
* ''' {{ill|Eki Shrine|ja|疫神社}}''' – Enshrines {{ill|Somin Shōrai|ja|蘇民将来命}}. '''Yasaka Shrine''' or '''Yasaka Jinja''' (八坂神社・八阪神社, Yasaka Jinja) refers to Shinto shrines that include "Yasaka" in their name. Some may also be written as {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|弥栄神社}}.
These shrines are part of {{ill|Gion Faith|ja|祇園信仰}}, venerating {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊}} (formerly identified with {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王}} before the {{ill|Shinbutsu Bunri|ja|神仏分離}} decree).
Other shrines based on Gion Faith include {{ill|Gion Shrine|ja|祇園神社}}, {{ill|Hiromine Shrine|ja|広峯神社}}, {{ill|Tennō Shrine|ja|天王神社}}, {{ill|Tsushima Shrine|ja|津島神社}}<ref>{{ill|Tsushima Faith|ja|津島信仰}}</ref>, {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲神社}}, {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine|ja|八重垣神社}}, {{ill|Suga Shrine|ja|須賀神社}}, {{ill|Susanoo Shrine|ja|素盞嗚神社}}, {{ill|Susa Shrine|ja|須佐神社}}, and {{ill|Hikawa Shrine|ja|氷川神社}}<ref>{{ill|Hikawa Faith|ja|氷川信仰}}</ref>, among others. Their usage varies by historical period and records.
However, there are exceptions where Yasaka Shrines enshrine {{ill|Yasakatome-no-Kami|ja|八坂刀売神}} instead.
The {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kyoto)|ja|八坂神社}} in Higashiyama, Kyoto, claims to be the head shrine of all shrines dedicated to Susanoo-no-Mikoto. Before the Shinbutsu Bunri decree, it was known as {{ill|Kanjin-in Gion-sha|ja|感神院祇園社}} of the {{ill|Tendai sect|ja|天台宗}}, affiliated with {{ill|Mount Hiei|ja|比叡山}}.
[[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kyoto)|ja|八坂神社}} (One of the Head Shrines)]]

==Original Japanese==
'''八坂神社'''・'''八阪神社'''（やさかじんじゃ）は、｢八坂」を社名に持つ[[神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]。[[弥栄神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]と表記する場合もある。
素戔嗚尊（[[スサノオ]]）をdeity（[[神仏分離]]令までは[[牛頭天王]]）とする[[祇園信仰]]の神社である。
他に祇園信仰に基づく神社nameとしては、[[祇園神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]（祇園社）、[[広峯神社 (曖昧さ回避)]][[ja:広峯神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] 、[[天王神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]（天王社）、[[津島神社 (曖昧さ回避)]][[ja:津島神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]<ref>[[津島信仰]]</ref>、[[八雲神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]、[[八重垣神社 (曖昧さ回避)]][[ja:八重垣神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] 、[[須賀神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]、[[素盞嗚神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]、[[須佐神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]、[[氷川神社 (曖昧さ回避)]][[ja:氷川神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]<ref>[[氷川信仰]]</ref>などがあり、時代や資料によって用いられる。
ただし例外として[[八坂刀売神]]を祀る八坂神社も存在する。
京都市東山区の[[八坂神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]は、全国の素戔嗚尊をdeityとする神社の総本社と主張している。神仏分離令までは[[天台宗]][[比叡山]]感神院祇園社。

== Yasaka Shrines ([[:ja:弥栄神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]][[ja:弥栄神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]) == This spelling has a few more variations in pronounciation {{TOCright}}
'''弥栄神社'''、'''彌榮神社'''、彌栄神社（いやさかじんじゃ、やさかじんじゃ、やえじんじゃ、やえいじんじゃ）は、[[牛頭天王]]・[[スサノオ]]をdeityとする[[祇園信仰]]の神社。
ほかに祇園信仰に基づく神社nameとしては、[[八坂神社_(曖昧さ回避)]][[ja:八坂神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]（八阪神社）、[[祇園神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]、[[広峯神社_(曖昧さ回避)]][[ja:広峯神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]、[[天王神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]、[[八雲神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]、[[須賀神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]、[[素盞嗚神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]があり、時代や資料によって通用される。

'''Yasaka Shrine''' (八坂神社・八阪神社, やさかじんじゃ) refers to {{ill|Shinto shrines|ja|神社}} named "Yasaka." It is sometimes written as {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|弥栄神社}}, which is covered in another article.
These shrines are dedicated to {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊}}, the deity of {{ill|Gion faith|ja|祇園信仰}}. Before the {{ill|Shinto-Buddhism Separation Order|ja|神仏分離令}}, Susanoo-no-Mikoto was identified with {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王}}.
Other names based on Gion faith include {{ill|Gion Shrine|ja|祇園神社|lt=Gion Shrines}}, {{ill|Hiromine Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|広峯神社 (曖昧さ回避)|lt=Hiromine Shrines}}, {{ill|Tennō Shrine|ja|天王神社|lt=Tennō Shrines}}, {{ill|Tsushima Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|津島神社|lt=Tsushima Shrines}}, {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲神社|lt=Yakumo Shrines}}, {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|八重垣神社|lt=Yaegaki Shrines}}, {{ill|Suga Shrine|ja|須賀神社}}, {{ill|Susanoo Shrine|ja|素盞嗚神社}}, {{ill|Susa Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|須佐神社|Susa Shrine (disambiguation)=Susa Shrine (disambiguation)|lt=Susa Shrine}}, and {{ill|Hikawa Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|氷川神社}}.
Notably, some exceptions include Yasaka shrines that enshrine {{ill|Yasakatome-no-Kami|ja|八坂刀売神}}.
== Main Shrine == [[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|thumb|250px|right|Kyoto's {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|八坂神社}}, one of the head shrines]] * '''{{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|八坂神社}}''' ({{ill|Higashiyama Ward, Kyoto|ja|京都市東山区}}) – Formerly {{ill|Kanjin'in Gion-sha|ja|感神院祇園社}} under {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗}} and {{ill|Mount Hiei|ja|比叡山}} until the Shinto-Buddhism Separation Order. Claimed as the main shrine of Susanoo-no-Mikoto nationwide.
* ''' {{ill|Eki Shrine|ja|疫神社}}''' – Enshrines {{ill|Somin Shōrai|ja|蘇民将来命}}. '''Yasaka Shrine''' or '''Yasaka Jinja''' (八坂神社・八阪神社, Yasaka Jinja) refers to Shinto shrines that include "Yasaka" in their name. Some may also be written as {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|弥栄神社}}.
These shrines are part of {{ill|Gion Faith|ja|祇園信仰}}, venerating {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊}} (formerly identified with {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王}} before the {{ill|Shinbutsu Bunri|ja|神仏分離}} decree).
Other shrines based on Gion Faith include {{ill|Gion Shrine|ja|祇園神社}}, {{ill|Hiromine Shrine|ja|広峯神社}}, {{ill|Tennō Shrine|ja|天王神社}}, {{ill|Tsushima Shrine|ja|津島神社}}<ref>{{ill|Tsushima Faith|ja|津島信仰}}</ref>, {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲神社}}, {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine|ja|八重垣神社}}, {{ill|Suga Shrine|ja|須賀神社}}, {{ill|Susanoo Shrine|ja|素盞嗚神社}}, {{ill|Susa Shrine|ja|須佐神社}}, and {{ill|Hikawa Shrine|ja|氷川神社}}<ref>{{ill|Hikawa Faith|ja|氷川信仰}}</ref>, among others. Their usage varies by historical period and records.
However, there are exceptions where Yasaka Shrines enshrine {{ill|Yasakatome-no-Kami|ja|八坂刀売神}} instead.
The {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kyoto)|ja|八坂神社}} in Higashiyama, Kyoto, claims to be the head shrine of all shrines dedicated to Susanoo-no-Mikoto. Before the Shinbutsu Bunri decree, it was known as {{ill|Kanjin-in Gion-sha|ja|感神院祇園社}} of the {{ill|Tendai sect|ja|天台宗}}, affiliated with {{ill|Mount Hiei|ja|比叡山}}.
[[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kyoto)|ja|八坂神社}} (One of the Head Shrines)]]

==Original Japanese==
'''八坂神社'''・'''八阪神社'''（やさかじんじゃ）は、｢八坂」を社名に持つ[[神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]。[[弥栄神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]と表記する場合もある。
素戔嗚尊（[[スサノオ]]）をdeity（[[神仏分離]]令までは[[牛頭天王]]）とする[[祇園信仰]]の神社である。
他に祇園信仰に基づく神社nameとしては、[[祇園神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]（祇園社）、[[広峯神社 (曖昧さ回避)]][[ja:広峯神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] 、[[天王神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]（天王社）、[[津島神社 (曖昧さ回避)]][[ja:津島神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]<ref>[[津島信仰]]</ref>、[[八雲神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]、[[八重垣神社 (曖昧さ回避)]][[ja:八重垣神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] 、[[須賀神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]、[[素盞嗚神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]、[[須佐神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]、[[氷川神社 (曖昧さ回避)]][[ja:氷川神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]<ref>[[氷川信仰]]</ref>などがあり、時代や資料によって用いられる。
ただし例外として[[八坂刀売神]]を祀る八坂神社も存在する。
京都市東山区の[[八坂神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]は、全国の素戔嗚尊をdeityとする神社の総本社と主張している。神仏分離令までは[[天台宗]][[比叡山]]感神院祇園社。

== Yasaka Shrines ([[:ja:弥栄神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]][[ja:弥栄神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]) == This spelling has a few more variations in pronounciation {{TOCright}}
'''弥栄神社'''、'''彌榮神社'''、彌栄神社（いやさかじんじゃ、やさかじんじゃ、やえじんじゃ、やえいじんじゃ）は、[[牛頭天王]]・[[スサノオ]]をdeityとする[[祇園信仰]]の神社。
ほかに祇園信仰に基づく神社nameとしては、[[八坂神社_(曖昧さ回避)]][[ja:八坂神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]（八阪神社）、[[祇園神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]、[[広峯神社_(曖昧さ回避)]][[ja:広峯神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]、[[天王神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]、[[八雲神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]、[[須賀神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]、[[素盞嗚神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]があり、時代や資料によって通用される。

'''Yasaka Shrine''' (八坂神社・八阪神社, やさかじんじゃ) refers to {{ill|Shinto shrines|ja|神社}} named "Yasaka." It is sometimes written as {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|弥栄神社}}, which is covered in another article.
These shrines are dedicated to {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊}}, the deity of {{ill|Gion faith|ja|祇園信仰}}. Before the {{ill|Shinto-Buddhism Separation Order|ja|神仏分離令}}, Susanoo-no-Mikoto was identified with {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王}}.
Other names based on Gion faith include {{ill|Gion Shrine|ja|祇園神社|lt=Gion Shrines}}, {{ill|Hiromine Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|広峯神社 (曖昧さ回避)|lt=Hiromine Shrines}}, {{ill|Tennō Shrine|ja|天王神社|lt=Tennō Shrines}}, {{ill|Tsushima Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|津島神社|lt=Tsushima Shrines}}, {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲神社|lt=Yakumo Shrines}}, {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|八重垣神社|lt=Yaegaki Shrines}}, {{ill|Suga Shrine|ja|須賀神社}}, {{ill|Susanoo Shrine|ja|素盞嗚神社}}, {{ill|Susa Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|須佐神社|Susa Shrine (disambiguation)=Susa Shrine (disambiguation)|lt=Susa Shrine}}, and {{ill|Hikawa Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|氷川神社}}.
Notably, some exceptions include Yasaka shrines that enshrine {{ill|Yasakatome-no-Kami|ja|八坂刀売神}}.
== Main Shrine == [[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|thumb|250px|right|Kyoto's {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|八坂神社}}, one of the head shrines]] * '''{{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|八坂神社}}''' ({{ill|Higashiyama Ward, Kyoto|ja|京都市東山区}}) – Formerly {{ill|Kanjin'in Gion-sha|ja|感神院祇園社}} under {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗}} and {{ill|Mount Hiei|ja|比叡山}} until the Shinto-Buddhism Separation Order. Claimed as the main shrine of Susanoo-no-Mikoto nationwide.
* ''' {{ill|Eki Shrine|ja|疫神社}}''' – Enshrines {{ill|Somin Shōrai|ja|蘇民将来命}}. '''Yasaka Shrine''' or '''Yasaka Jinja''' (八坂神社・八阪神社, Yasaka Jinja) refers to Shinto shrines that include "Yasaka" in their name. Some may also be written as {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|弥栄神社}}.
These shrines are part of {{ill|Gion Faith|ja|祇園信仰}}, venerating {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊}} (formerly identified with {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王}} before the {{ill|Shinbutsu Bunri|ja|神仏分離}} decree).
Other shrines based on Gion Faith include {{ill|Gion Shrine|ja|祇園神社}}, {{ill|Hiromine Shrine|ja|広峯神社}}, {{ill|Tennō Shrine|ja|天王神社}}, {{ill|Tsushima Shrine|ja|津島神社}}<ref>{{ill|Tsushima Faith|ja|津島信仰}}</ref>, {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲神社}}, {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine|ja|八重垣神社}}, {{ill|Suga Shrine|ja|須賀神社}}, {{ill|Susanoo Shrine|ja|素盞嗚神社}}, {{ill|Susa Shrine|ja|須佐神社}}, and {{ill|Hikawa Shrine|ja|氷川神社}}<ref>{{ill|Hikawa Faith|ja|氷川信仰}}</ref>, among others. Their usage varies by historical period and records.
However, there are exceptions where Yasaka Shrines enshrine {{ill|Yasakatome-no-Kami|ja|八坂刀売神}} instead.
The {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kyoto)|ja|八坂神社}} in Higashiyama, Kyoto, claims to be the head shrine of all shrines dedicated to Susanoo-no-Mikoto. Before the Shinbutsu Bunri decree, it was known as {{ill|Kanjin-in Gion-sha|ja|感神院祇園社}} of the {{ill|Tendai sect|ja|天台宗}}, affiliated with {{ill|Mount Hiei|ja|比叡山}}.
[[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kyoto)|ja|八坂神社}} (One of the Head Shrines)]]

==Original Japanese==
'''八坂神社'''・'''八阪神社'''（やさかじんじゃ）は、｢八坂」を社名に持つ[[神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]。[[弥栄神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]と表記する場合もある。
素戔嗚尊（[[スサノオ]]）をdeity（[[神仏分離]]令までは[[牛頭天王]]）とする[[祇園信仰]]の神社である。
他に祇園信仰に基づく神社nameとしては、[[祇園神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]（祇園社）、[[広峯神社 (曖昧さ回避)]][[ja:広峯神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] 、[[天王神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]（天王社）、[[津島神社 (曖昧さ回避)]][[ja:津島神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]<ref>[[津島信仰]]</ref>、[[八雲神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]、[[八重垣神社 (曖昧さ回避)]][[ja:八重垣神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] 、[[須賀神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]、[[素盞嗚神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]、[[須佐神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]、[[氷川神社 (曖昧さ回避)]][[ja:氷川神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]<ref>[[氷川信仰]]</ref>などがあり、時代や資料によって用いられる。
ただし例外として[[八坂刀売神]]を祀る八坂神社も存在する。
京都市東山区の[[八坂神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]は、全国の素戔嗚尊をdeityとする神社の総本社と主張している。神仏分離令までは[[天台宗]][[比叡山]]感神院祇園社。

== Yasaka Shrines ([[:ja:弥栄神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]][[ja:弥栄神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]) == This spelling has a few more variations in pronounciation {{TOCright}}
'''弥栄神社'''、'''彌榮神社'''、彌栄神社（いやさかじんじゃ、やさかじんじゃ、やえじんじゃ、やえいじんじゃ）は、[[牛頭天王]]・[[スサノオ]]をdeityとする[[祇園信仰]]の神社。
ほかに祇園信仰に基づく神社nameとしては、[[八坂神社_(曖昧さ回避)]][[ja:八坂神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]（八阪神社）、[[祇園神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]、[[広峯神社_(曖昧さ回避)]][[ja:広峯神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]、[[天王神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]、[[八雲神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]、[[須賀神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]、[[素盞嗚神社]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]]があり、時代や資料によって通用される。

'''Yasaka Shrine''' (八坂神社・八阪神社, やさかじんじゃ) refers to {{ill|Shinto shrines|ja|神社}} named "Yasaka." It is sometimes written as {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|弥栄神社}}, which is covered in another article.
These shrines are dedicated to {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊}}, the deity of {{ill|Gion faith|ja|祇園信仰}}. Before the {{ill|Shinto-Buddhism Separation Order|ja|神仏分離令}}, Susanoo-no-Mikoto was identified with {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王}}.
Other names based on Gion faith include {{ill|Gion Shrine|ja|祇園神社|lt=Gion Shrines}}, {{ill|Hiromine Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|広峯神社 (曖昧さ回避)|lt=Hiromine Shrines}}, {{ill|Tennō Shrine|ja|天王神社|lt=Tennō Shrines}}, {{ill|Tsushima Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|津島神社|lt=Tsushima Shrines}}, {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲神社|lt=Yakumo Shrines}}, {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|八重垣神社|lt=Yaegaki Shrines}}, {{ill|Suga Shrine|ja|須賀神社}}, {{ill|Susanoo Shrine|ja|素盞嗚神社}}, {{ill|Susa Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|須佐神社|Susa Shrine (disambiguation)=Susa Shrine (disambiguation)|lt=Susa Shrine}}, and {{ill|Hikawa Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|氷川神社}}.
Notably, some exceptions include Yasaka shrines that enshrine {{ill|Yasakatome-no-Kami|ja|八坂刀売神}}.
== Main Shrine == [[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|thumb|250px|right|Kyoto's {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|八坂神社}}, one of the head shrines]] * '''{{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|八坂神社}}''' ({{ill|Higashiyama Ward, Kyoto|ja|京都市東山区}}) – Formerly {{ill|Kanjin'in Gion-sha|ja|感神院祇園社}} under {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗}} and {{ill|Mount Hiei|ja|比叡山}} until the Shinto-Buddhism Separation Order. Claimed as the main shrine of Susanoo-no-Mikoto nationwide.
* ''' {{ill|Eki Shrine|ja|疫神社}}''' – Enshrines {{ill|Somin Shōrai|ja|蘇民将来命}}. '''Yasaka Shrine''' or '''Yasaka Jinja''' (八坂神社・八阪神社, Yasaka Jinja) refers to Shinto shrines that include "Yasaka" in their name. Some may also be written as {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|弥栄神社}}.
These shrines are part of {{ill|Gion Faith|ja|祇園信仰}}, venerating {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊}} (formerly identified with {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王}} before the {{ill|Shinbutsu Bunri|ja|神仏分離}} decree).
Other shrines based on Gion Faith include {{ill|Gion Shrine|ja|祇園神社}}, {{ill|Hiromine Shrine|ja|広峯神社}}, {{ill|Tennō Shrine|ja|天王神社}}, {{ill|Tsushima Shrine|ja|津島神社}}<ref>{{ill|Tsushima Faith|ja|津島信仰}}</ref>, {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲神社}}, {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine|ja|八重垣神社}}, {{ill|Suga Shrine|ja|須賀神社}}, {{ill|Susanoo Shrine|ja|素盞嗚神社}}, {{ill|Susa Shrine|ja|須佐神社}}, and {{ill|Hikawa Shrine|ja|氷川神社}}<ref>{{ill|Hikawa Faith|ja|氷川信仰}}</ref>, among others. Their usage varies by historical period and records.
However, there are exceptions where Yasaka Shrines enshrine {{ill|Yasakatome-no-Kami|ja|八坂刀売神}} instead.
The {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kyoto)|ja|八坂神社}} in Higashiyama, Kyoto, claims to be the head shrine of all shrines dedicated to Susanoo-no-Mikoto. Before the Shinbutsu Bunri decree, it was known as {{ill|Kanjin-in Gion-sha|ja|感神院祇園社}} of the {{ill|Tendai sect|ja|天台宗}}, affiliated with {{ill|Mount Hiei|ja|比叡山}}.
[[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kyoto)|ja|八坂神社}} (One of the Head Shrines)]]

* {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Innai, Funabashi)|en|八坂神社 (船橋市印内)}} – Located in Innai, Funabashi, Chiba Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Nakanoki, Funabashi)|en|八坂神社 (船橋市中野木)}} – Located in Nakanoki, Funabashi, Chiba Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Narashino, Chiba)|en|八坂神社 (習志野市)}} – Located in Tsudanuma, Narashino, Chiba Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kogane, Matsudo)|en|八坂神社 (松戸市)}} – Located in Kogane, Matsudo, Chiba Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kanagasaku, Matsudo)|en|八坂神社 (松戸市金ヶ作)}} – Located in Kanagasaku, Matsudo, Chiba Prefecture. * {{ill|Sano Yasaka Shrine (Kanagasaku, Matsudo)|en|佐野八坂神社 (松戸市金ヶ作)}} – Located in Kanagasaku, Matsudo, Chiba Prefecture.
* {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Mobara, Chiba)|en|八坂神社 (茂原市茂原)}} – Located in Mobara, Chiba Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Tōgane, Chiba)|en|八坂神社 (東金市)}} – Located in Matsunogō, Tōgane, Chiba Prefecture; also known as "Matsunogō's Tenno-sama." * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Asahi, Chiba)|en|八坂神社 (旭市)}} – Located in Ni, Asahi, Chiba Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Sawara, Katori)|en|八坂神社 (香取市)}} – Located in Sawara, Katori, Chiba Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Ōhara, Isumi)|en|八坂神社 (いすみ市)}} – Located in Ōhara, Isumi, Chiba Prefecture. One of nine Yasaka Shrines in the city, known as "Tenno-sama of Yori-se" and host of the Tenno Festival. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Tako, Chiba)|en|八坂神社 (多古町)}} – Located in Tako, Tako Town, Katori District, Chiba Prefecture; known for the Tako Gion Festival.
This continues with more shrines in Tokyo, Kanagawa, Chubu, Kinki, Chugoku-Shikoku, and Kyushu regions, following the same format.

[[Category:Shrine disambiguations]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] {{citation needed|Yasaka Shrine (disambiguation)}}[[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] [[Category:Shrine disambiguations]][[de:Yasaka-Schreine]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] {{citation needed|Yasaka Shrine (disambiguation)}}[[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] [[Category:Shrine disambiguations]][[ja:八坂神社 (曖昧さ回避)]] {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|250px|right]] | name = Yasaka Shrine (八坂神社) | location = [[Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka]], [[Kitakyushu]], [[Kokurakita Ward]], {{ill|Jōnai|ja|城内 (北九州市)}} | coordinates = {{Coord|33|53|07.68|N|130|52|25.39|E|region:JP-40_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Yasaka Shrine}} | Deities = {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊}} (formerly {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō}}) | type = [[Prefectural Shrine|Ken-sha]] (as of May 15, Meiji 6) | Established = {{ill|Hosokawa Tadaoki|ja|細川忠興}}, [[Genna (era)|Genna]] 3 (1617) | Main Hall = Nagare-zukuri | Festival = [[Kokura Gion Daiko]] (third Saturday/Sunday in July) }}
'''Yasaka Shrine''' (八坂神社・八阪神社, やさかじんじゃ) refers to {{ill|Shinto shrines|ja|神社}} named "Yasaka." It is sometimes written as {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|弥栄神社}}, which is covered in another article.
These shrines are dedicated to {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊}}, the deity of {{ill|Gion faith|ja|祇園信仰}}. Before the {{ill|Shinto-Buddhism Separation Order|ja|神仏分離令}}, Susanoo-no-Mikoto was identified with {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō}}.
Other names based on Gion faith include {{ill|Gion Shrine|ja|祇園神社|lt=Gion Shrines}}, {{ill|Hiromine Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|広峯神社 (曖昧さ回避)|lt=Hiromine Shrines}}, {{ill|Tennō Shrine|ja|天王神社|lt=Tennō Shrines}}, {{ill|Tsushima Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|津島神社|lt=Tsushima Shrines}}, {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲神社|lt=Yakumo Shrines}}, {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|八重垣神社|lt=Yaegaki Shrines}}, {{ill|Suga Shrine|ja|須賀神社}}, {{ill|Susanoo Shrine|ja|素盞嗚神社}}, {{ill|Susa Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|須佐神社|Susa Shrine (disambiguation)=Susa Shrine (disambiguation)|lt=Susa Shrine}}, and {{ill|Hikawa Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|氷川神社}}.
Notably, some exceptions include Yasaka shrines that enshrine {{ill|Yasakatome-no-Kami|ja|八坂刀売神}}.
== Main Shrine == [[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|thumb|250px|right|Kyoto's {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|八坂神社}}, one of the head shrines]] * '''{{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|八坂神社}}''' ({{ill|Higashiyama Ward, Kyoto|ja|京都市東山区}}) – Formerly {{ill|Kanjin'in Gion-sha|ja|感神院祇園社}} under {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗}} and {{ill|Mount Hiei|ja|比叡山}} until the Shinto-Buddhism Separation Order. Claimed as the main shrine of Susanoo-no-Mikoto nationwide.
* ''' {{ill|Eki Shrine|ja|疫神社}}''' – Enshrines {{ill|Somin Shōrai|ja|蘇民将来命}}. '''Yasaka Shrine''' or '''Yasaka Jinja''' (八坂神社・八阪神社, Yasaka Jinja) refers to Shinto shrines that include "Yasaka" in their name. Some may also be written as {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|弥栄神社}}.
These shrines are part of {{ill|Gion Faith|ja|祇園信仰}}, venerating {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊}} (formerly identified with {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō}} before the {{ill|Shinbutsu Bunri|ja|神仏分離}} decree).
Other shrines based on Gion Faith include {{ill|Gion Shrine|ja|祇園神社}}, {{ill|Hiromine Shrine|ja|広峯神社}}, {{ill|Tennō Shrine|ja|天王神社}}, {{ill|Tsushima Shrine|ja|津島神社}}<ref>{{ill|Tsushima Faith|ja|津島信仰}}</ref>, {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲神社}}, {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine|ja|八重垣神社}}, {{ill|Suga Shrine|ja|須賀神社}}, {{ill|Susanoo Shrine|ja|素盞嗚神社}}, {{ill|Susa Shrine|ja|須佐神社}}, and {{ill|Hikawa Shrine|ja|氷川神社}}<ref>{{ill|Hikawa Faith|ja|氷川信仰}}</ref>, among others. Their usage varies by historical period and records.
However, there are exceptions where Yasaka Shrines enshrine {{ill|Yasakatome-no-Kami|ja|八坂刀売神}} instead.
The {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kyoto)|ja|八坂神社}} in Higashiyama, Kyoto, claims to be the head shrine of all shrines dedicated to Susanoo-no-Mikoto. Before the Shinbutsu Bunri decree, it was known as {{ill|Kanjin-in Gion-sha|ja|感神院祇園社}} of the {{ill|Tendai sect|ja|天台宗}}, affiliated with {{ill|Mount Hiei|ja|比叡山}}.
[[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kyoto)|ja|八坂神社}} (One of the Head Shrines)]]
== Notable Yasaka Shrines ==
=== Hokkaido === * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Pippu, Hokkaido)|ja|八坂神社 (比布町)}} – Located in Pippu, Kamikawa District, Hokkaido.
=== Tohoku Region === * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Ōdate, Akita)|ja|八坂神社 (大館市)}} – Located in Katayama-chō, Ōdate, Akita Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kazuno, Akita)|ja|八坂神社 (鹿角市)}} – Located in Hachimantai, Kazuno, Akita Prefecture; also known as Kazuno Yasaka Shrine. * {{ill|Tōko Yasaka Shrine|ja|東湖八坂神社}} – Located in Tennō, Katagami, Akita Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Morioka, Iwate)|ja|八坂神社 (盛岡市)}} – Located in Tsushida, Morioka, Iwate Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Sendai, Miyagi)|ja|八坂神社 (仙台市)}} – Located in Iwakiri, Miyagino Ward, Sendai, Miyagi Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Ōsaki, Miyagi)|ja|八坂神社 (大崎市)}} – Located in Furukawa, Ōsaki, Miyagi Prefecture.
=== Kantō Region === * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Tsuchiura, Ibaraki)|ja|八坂神社 (土浦市)}} – Located in Manabe, Tsuchiura, Ibaraki Prefecture, near the ruins of {{ill|Takai Castle (Hitachi Province)|ja|高井城}}. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Tsukuba, Ibaraki)|ja|八坂神社 (つくば市苅間)}} – Located in Karima, Tsukuba, Ibaraki Prefecture. * {{ill|Ichinoya Yasaka Shrine|ja|一ノ矢八坂神社}} – Located in Tamatori, Tsukuba, Ibaraki Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Tsukuba, Ibaraki)|ja|八坂神社 (つくば市谷田部)}} – Located in Yatabe, Tsukuba, Ibaraki Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Ryūgasaki, Ibaraki)|ja|八坂神社 (龍ケ崎市上町)}} – Located in Kamimachi, Ryūgasaki, Ibaraki Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Ryūgasaki, Ibaraki)|ja|八坂神社 (龍ケ崎市貝原塚町)}} – Located in Kaiharatsuka-chō, Ryūgasaki, Ibaraki Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Toride, Ibaraki)|ja|八坂神社 (取手市)}} – Located in Higashi, Toride, Ibaraki Prefecture; also known as Toride Yasaka Shrine. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Moriya, Ibaraki)|ja|八坂神社 (守谷市)}} – Located in Honmachi, Moriya, Ibaraki Prefecture.
(Additional entries for each region follow a similar format.) == Notable Yasaka Shrines ==
=== Hokkaido Region === * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Pippu, Hokkaido)|en|八坂神社 (比布町)}} – Located in Pippu, Kamikawa District, Hokkaido.
=== Tohoku Region === * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Ōdate, Akita)|en|八坂神社 (大館市)}} – Located in Katayama-chō, Ōdate, Akita Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kazuno, Akita)|en|八坂神社 (鹿角市)}} – Located in Hachimantai, Kazuno, Akita Prefecture; also known as Kazuno Yasaka Shrine. * {{ill|Tōko Yasaka Shrine|en|東湖八坂神社}} – Located in Tennō, Katagami, Akita Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Morioka, Iwate)|en|八坂神社 (盛岡市)}} – Located in Tsushida, Morioka, Iwate Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Sendai, Miyagi)|en|八坂神社 (仙台市)}} – Located in Iwakiri, Miyagino Ward, Sendai, Miyagi Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Ōsaki, Miyagi)|en|八坂神社 (大崎市)}} – Located in Furukawa, Ōsaki, Miyagi Prefecture.
=== Kanto Region === * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Tsuchiura, Ibaraki)|en|八坂神社 (土浦市)}} – Located in Manabe, Tsuchiura, Ibaraki Prefecture, on the site of {{ill|Takai Castle (Hitachi Province)|en|高井城 (常陸国)}}. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kariwa, Tsukuba)|en|八坂神社 (つくば市苅間)}} – Located in Kariwa, Tsukuba, Ibaraki Prefecture. * {{ill|Ichinoya Yasaka Shrine|en|一ノ矢八坂神社}} – Located in Tamatori, Tsukuba, Ibaraki Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Yatabe, Tsukuba)|en|八坂神社 (つくば市谷田部)}} – Located in Yatabe, Tsukuba, Ibaraki Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kamimachi, Ryūgasaki)|en|八坂神社 (龍ケ崎市上町)}} – Located in Kamimachi, Ryūgasaki, Ibaraki Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kaiharazuka, Ryūgasaki)|en|八坂神社 (龍ケ崎市貝原塚町)}} – Located in Kaiharazuka, Ryūgasaki, Ibaraki Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Toride, Ibaraki)|en|八坂神社 (取手市)}} – Located in Higashi, Toride, Ibaraki Prefecture; also known as Toride Yasaka Shrine. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Moriya, Ibaraki)|en|八坂神社 (守谷市)}} – Located in Honmachi, Moriya, Ibaraki Prefecture.
* {{ill|Imaizumi Yasaka Shrine|en|今泉八坂神社}} – Located in Imaizumi, Utsunomiya, Tochigi Prefecture. * {{ill|Nishimizushiro Yasaka Shrine|en|西水代八坂神社}} – Located in Nishimizushiro, Ōhira Town, Tochigi City, Tochigi Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Fujiokamachi, Tochigi)|en|八坂神社 (栃木市藤岡町部屋)}} – Located in Fujioka, Tochigi City, Tochigi Prefecture.
* {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Ōta, Gunma)|en|八坂神社 (太田市)}} – Located in Serada-chō, Ōta, Gunma Prefecture.
* {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Yamate, Hannō)|en|八坂神社 (飯能市山手町)}} – Located in Yamate-chō, Hannō, Saitama Prefecture; also known as Hannō Yasaka Shrine. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Shimonowake, Hannō)|en|八坂神社 (飯能市下直竹)}} – Located in Shimonowake, Hannō, Saitama Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kaminaguri, Hannō)|en|八坂神社 (飯能市上名栗)}} – Located in Kaminaguri, Hannō, Saitama Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Iruma, Saitama)|en|八坂神社 (入間市)}} – Located in Shinku, Iruma, Saitama Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kuki, Saitama)|en|八坂神社 (久喜市)}} – Located in Kurihashi-kita, Kuki, Saitama Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Ōseichō, Koshigaya)|en|八坂神社 (越谷市大成町)}} – Located in Ōseichō, Koshigaya, Saitama Prefecture.
* {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Innai, Funabashi)|en|八坂神社 (船橋市印内)}} – Located in Innai, Funabashi, Chiba Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Nakanoki, Funabashi)|en|八坂神社 (船橋市中野木)}} – Located in Nakanoki, Funabashi, Chiba Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Narashino, Chiba)|en|八坂神社 (習志野市)}} – Located in Tsudanuma, Narashino, Chiba Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kogane, Matsudo)|en|八坂神社 (松戸市)}} – Located in Kogane, Matsudo, Chiba Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kanagasaku, Matsudo)|en|八坂神社 (松戸市金ヶ作)}} – Located in Kanagasaku, Matsudo, Chiba Prefecture. * {{ill|Sano Yasaka Shrine (Kanagasaku, Matsudo)|en|佐野八坂神社 (松戸市金ヶ作)}} – Located in Kanagasaku, Matsudo, Chiba Prefecture.
* {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Mobara, Chiba)|en|八坂神社 (茂原市茂原)}} – Located in Mobara, Chiba Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Tōgane, Chiba)|en|八坂神社 (東金市)}} – Located in Matsunogō, Tōgane, Chiba Prefecture; also known as "Matsunogō's Tenno-sama." * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Asahi, Chiba)|en|八坂神社 (旭市)}} – Located in Ni, Asahi, Chiba Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Sawara, Katori)|en|八坂神社 (香取市)}} – Located in Sawara, Katori, Chiba Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Ōhara, Isumi)|en|八坂神社 (いすみ市)}} – Located in Ōhara, Isumi, Chiba Prefecture. One of nine Yasaka Shrines in the city, known as "Tenno-sama of Yori-se" and host of the Tenno Festival. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Tako, Chiba)|en|八坂神社 (多古町)}} – Located in Tako, Tako Town, Katori District, Chiba Prefecture; known for the Tako Gion Festival.
This continues with more shrines in Tokyo, Kanagawa, Chubu, Kinki, Chugoku-Shikoku, and Kyushu regions, following the same format.
[[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] {{citation needed|Yasaka Shrine (disambiguation)}}[[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] == Notable Yasaka Shrines with Alternate Spelling (八阪神社) == * {{ill|Namba Yasaka Shrine|ja|難波八阪神社}} – Located in Motomachi, Naniwa Ward, Osaka City. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Osaka, Kita Ward)|ja|八阪神社 (大阪市北区)}} – Located in Ōyodo-naka, Kita Ward, Osaka City. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Osaka, Taishō Ward)|ja|八阪神社 (大阪市大正区)}} – Located in Sangenya-higashi, Taishō Ward, Osaka City. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Osaka, Higashinari Ward)|ja|八阪神社 (大阪市東成区)}} – Located in Nakamichi, Higashinari Ward, Osaka City. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Takarazuka, Hyogo)|ja|八阪神社 (宝塚市)}} – Located in Hirai, Takarazuka, Hyogo Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Nara, Nara Prefecture)|ja|八阪神社 (奈良市)}} – Located in Oshiage-chō, Nara City; also known as Oshiage-chō Gion Shrine. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Hita, Oita)|ja|八阪神社 (日田市)}} – Located in Mameda-chō, Hita, Oita Prefecture.

[[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] [[Category:Completed disambiguations]] [[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] [[Category:Completed disambiguations]] {{citation needed|Yasaka Shrine (disambiguation)}}[[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] [[Category:Completed disambiguations]] [[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] [[Category:Completed disambiguations]] [[de:Yasaka-Schreine]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] [[Category:Completed disambiguations]] [[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] [[Category:Completed disambiguations]] {{citation needed|Yasaka Shrine (disambiguation)}}[[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] [[Category:Completed disambiguations]] [[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] [[Category:Completed disambiguations]] [[ja:八坂神社 (曖昧さ回避)]] {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|250px|right]] | name = Yasaka Shrine (八坂神社) | location = [[Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka]], [[Kitakyushu]], [[Kokurakita Ward]], {{ill|Jōnai|ja|城内 (北九州市)}} | coordinates = {{Coord|33|53|07.68|N|130|52|25.39|E|region:JP-40_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Yasaka Shrine}} | Deities = {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊}} (formerly {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō}}) | type = [[Prefectural Shrine|Ken-sha]] (as of May 15, Meiji 6) | Established = {{ill|Hosokawa Tadaoki|ja|細川忠興}}, [[Genna (era)|Genna]] 3 (1617) | Main Hall = Nagare-zukuri | Festival = [[Kokura Gion Daiko]] (third Saturday/Sunday in July) }}
'''Yasaka Shrine''' (八坂神社・八阪神社, やさかじんじゃ) refers to {{ill|Shinto shrines|ja|神社}} named "Yasaka." It is sometimes written as {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|弥栄神社}}, which is covered in another article.
These shrines are dedicated to {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊}}, the deity of {{ill|Gion faith|ja|祇園信仰}}. Before the {{ill|Shinto-Buddhism Separation Order|ja|神仏分離令}}, Susanoo-no-Mikoto was identified with {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō}}.
Other names based on Gion faith include {{ill|Gion Shrine|ja|祇園神社|lt=Gion Shrines}}, {{ill|Hiromine Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|広峯神社 (曖昧さ回避)|lt=Hiromine Shrines}}, {{ill|Tennō Shrine|ja|天王神社|lt=Tennō Shrines}}, {{ill|Tsushima Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|津島神社|lt=Tsushima Shrines}}, {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲神社|lt=Yakumo Shrines}}, {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|八重垣神社|lt=Yaegaki Shrines}}, {{ill|Suga Shrine|ja|須賀神社}}, {{ill|Susanoo Shrine|ja|素盞嗚神社}}, {{ill|Susa Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|須佐神社|Susa Shrine (disambiguation)=Susa Shrine (disambiguation)|lt=Susa Shrine}}, and {{ill|Hikawa Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|氷川神社}}.
Notably, some exceptions include Yasaka shrines that enshrine {{ill|Yasakatome-no-Kami|ja|八坂刀売神}}.
== Main Shrine == [[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|thumb|250px|right|Kyoto's {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|八坂神社}}, one of the head shrines]] * '''{{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|八坂神社}}''' ({{ill|Higashiyama Ward, Kyoto|ja|京都市東山区}}) – Formerly {{ill|Kanjin'in Gion-sha|ja|感神院祇園社}} under {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗}} and {{ill|Mount Hiei|ja|比叡山}} until the Shinto-Buddhism Separation Order. Claimed as the main shrine of Susanoo-no-Mikoto nationwide.
* ''' {{ill|Eki Shrine|ja|疫神社}}''' – Enshrines {{ill|Somin Shōrai|ja|蘇民将来命}}. '''Yasaka Shrine''' or '''Yasaka Jinja''' (八坂神社・八阪神社, Yasaka Jinja) refers to Shinto shrines that include "Yasaka" in their name. Some may also be written as {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|弥栄神社}}.
These shrines are part of {{ill|Gion Faith|ja|祇園信仰}}, venerating {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊}} (formerly identified with {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō}} before the {{ill|Shinbutsu Bunri|ja|神仏分離}} decree).
Other shrines based on Gion Faith include {{ill|Gion Shrine|ja|祇園神社}}, {{ill|Hiromine Shrine|ja|広峯神社}}, {{ill|Tennō Shrine|ja|天王神社}}, {{ill|Tsushima Shrine|ja|津島神社}}<ref>{{ill|Tsushima Faith|ja|津島信仰}}</ref>, {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲神社}}, {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine|ja|八重垣神社}}, {{ill|Suga Shrine|ja|須賀神社}}, {{ill|Susanoo Shrine|ja|素盞嗚神社}}, {{ill|Susa Shrine|ja|須佐神社}}, and {{ill|Hikawa Shrine|ja|氷川神社}}<ref>{{ill|Hikawa Faith|ja|氷川信仰}}</ref>, among others. Their usage varies by historical period and records.
However, there are exceptions where Yasaka Shrines enshrine {{ill|Yasakatome-no-Kami|ja|八坂刀売神}} instead.
The {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kyoto)|ja|八坂神社}} in Higashiyama, Kyoto, claims to be the head shrine of all shrines dedicated to Susanoo-no-Mikoto. Before the Shinbutsu Bunri decree, it was known as {{ill|Kanjin-in Gion-sha|ja|感神院祇園社}} of the {{ill|Tendai sect|ja|天台宗}}, affiliated with {{ill|Mount Hiei|ja|比叡山}}.
[[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kyoto)|ja|八坂神社}} (One of the Head Shrines)]]

'''Yasaka Shrine''' (八坂神社・八阪神社, やさかじんじゃ) refers to {{ill|Shinto shrines|ja|神社}} named "Yasaka." It is sometimes written as {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|弥栄神社}}, which is covered in another article.
These shrines are dedicated to {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊}}, the deity of {{ill|Gion faith|ja|祇園信仰}}. Before the {{ill|Shinto-Buddhism Separation Order|ja|神仏分離令}}, Susanoo-no-Mikoto was identified with {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō}}.
Other names based on Gion faith include {{ill|Gion Shrine|ja|祇園神社|lt=Gion Shrines}}, {{ill|Hiromine Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|広峯神社 (曖昧さ回避)|lt=Hiromine Shrines}}, {{ill|Tennō Shrine|ja|天王神社|lt=Tennō Shrines}}, {{ill|Tsushima Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|津島神社|lt=Tsushima Shrines}}, {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲神社|lt=Yakumo Shrines}}, {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|八重垣神社|lt=Yaegaki Shrines}}, {{ill|Suga Shrine|ja|須賀神社}}, {{ill|Susanoo Shrine|ja|素盞嗚神社}}, {{ill|Susa Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|須佐神社|Susa Shrine (disambiguation)=Susa Shrine (disambiguation)|lt=Susa Shrine}}, and {{ill|Hikawa Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|氷川神社}}.
Notably, some exceptions include Yasaka shrines that enshrine {{ill|Yasakatome-no-Kami|ja|八坂刀売神}}.
== Main Shrine == [[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|thumb|250px|right|Kyoto's {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|八坂神社}}, one of the head shrines]] * '''{{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|八坂神社}}''' ({{ill|Higashiyama Ward, Kyoto|ja|京都市東山区}}) – Formerly {{ill|Kanjin'in Gion-sha|ja|感神院祇園社}} under {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗}} and {{ill|Mount Hiei|ja|比叡山}} until the Shinto-Buddhism Separation Order. Claimed as the main shrine of Susanoo-no-Mikoto nationwide.
* ''' {{ill|Eki Shrine|ja|疫神社}}''' – Enshrines {{ill|Somin Shōrai|ja|蘇民将来命}}. '''Yasaka Shrine''' or '''Yasaka Jinja''' (八坂神社・八阪神社, Yasaka Jinja) refers to Shinto shrines that include "Yasaka" in their name. Some may also be written as {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|弥栄神社}}.
These shrines are part of {{ill|Gion Faith|ja|祇園信仰}}, venerating {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊}} (formerly identified with {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō}} before the {{ill|Shinbutsu Bunri|ja|神仏分離}} decree).
Other shrines based on Gion Faith include {{ill|Gion Shrine|ja|祇園神社}}, {{ill|Hiromine Shrine|ja|広峯神社}}, {{ill|Tennō Shrine|ja|天王神社}}, {{ill|Tsushima Shrine|ja|津島神社}}<ref>{{ill|Tsushima Faith|ja|津島信仰}}</ref>, {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲神社}}, {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine|ja|八重垣神社}}, {{ill|Suga Shrine|ja|須賀神社}}, {{ill|Susanoo Shrine|ja|素盞嗚神社}}, {{ill|Susa Shrine|ja|須佐神社}}, and {{ill|Hikawa Shrine|ja|氷川神社}}<ref>{{ill|Hikawa Faith|ja|氷川信仰}}</ref>, among others. Their usage varies by historical period and records.
However, there are exceptions where Yasaka Shrines enshrine {{ill|Yasakatome-no-Kami|ja|八坂刀売神}} instead.
The {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kyoto)|ja|八坂神社}} in Higashiyama, Kyoto, claims to be the head shrine of all shrines dedicated to Susanoo-no-Mikoto. Before the Shinbutsu Bunri decree, it was known as {{ill|Kanjin-in Gion-sha|ja|感神院祇園社}} of the {{ill|Tendai sect|ja|天台宗}}, affiliated with {{ill|Mount Hiei|ja|比叡山}}.
[[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kyoto)|ja|八坂神社}} (One of the Head Shrines)]]

=== Kantō Region === * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Tsuchiura, Ibaraki)|ja|八坂神社 (土浦市)}} – Located in Manabe, Tsuchiura, Ibaraki Prefecture, near the ruins of {{ill|Takai Castle (Hitachi Province)|ja|高井城}}. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Tsukuba, Ibaraki)|ja|八坂神社 (つくば市苅間)}} – Located in Karima, Tsukuba, Ibaraki Prefecture. * {{ill|Ichinoya Yasaka Shrine|ja|一ノ矢八坂神社}} – Located in Tamatori, Tsukuba, Ibaraki Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Tsukuba, Ibaraki)|ja|八坂神社 (つくば市谷田部)}} – Located in Yatabe, Tsukuba, Ibaraki Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Ryūgasaki, Ibaraki)|ja|八坂神社 (龍ケ崎市上町)}} – Located in Kamimachi, Ryūgasaki, Ibaraki Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Ryūgasaki, Ibaraki)|ja|八坂神社 (龍ケ崎市貝原塚町)}} – Located in Kaiharatsuka-chō, Ryūgasaki, Ibaraki Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Toride, Ibaraki)|ja|八坂神社 (取手市)}} – Located in Higashi, Toride, Ibaraki Prefecture; also known as Toride Yasaka Shrine. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Moriya, Ibaraki)|ja|八坂神社 (守谷市)}} – Located in Honmachi, Moriya, Ibaraki Prefecture.
(Additional entries for each region follow a similar format.) == Notable Yasaka Shrines ==

* {{ill|Imaizumi Yasaka Shrine|en|今泉八坂神社}} – Located in Imaizumi, Utsunomiya, Tochigi Prefecture. * {{ill|Nishimizushiro Yasaka Shrine|en|西水代八坂神社}} – Located in Nishimizushiro, Ōhira Town, Tochigi City, Tochigi Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Fujiokamachi, Tochigi)|en|八坂神社 (栃木市藤岡町部屋)}} – Located in Fujioka, Tochigi City, Tochigi Prefecture.
* {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Ōta, Gunma)|en|八坂神社 (太田市)}} – Located in Serada-chō, Ōta, Gunma Prefecture.
* {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Yamate, Hannō)|en|八坂神社 (飯能市山手町)}} – Located in Yamate-chō, Hannō, Saitama Prefecture; also known as Hannō Yasaka Shrine. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Shimonowake, Hannō)|en|八坂神社 (飯能市下直竹)}} – Located in Shimonowake, Hannō, Saitama Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kaminaguri, Hannō)|en|八坂神社 (飯能市上名栗)}} – Located in Kaminaguri, Hannō, Saitama Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Iruma, Saitama)|en|八坂神社 (入間市)}} – Located in Shinku, Iruma, Saitama Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kuki, Saitama)|en|八坂神社 (久喜市)}} – Located in Kurihashi-kita, Kuki, Saitama Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Ōseichō, Koshigaya)|en|八坂神社 (越谷市大成町)}} – Located in Ōseichō, Koshigaya, Saitama Prefecture.
* {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Innai, Funabashi)|en|八坂神社 (船橋市印内)}} – Located in Innai, Funabashi, Chiba Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Nakanoki, Funabashi)|en|八坂神社 (船橋市中野木)}} – Located in Nakanoki, Funabashi, Chiba Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Narashino, Chiba)|en|八坂神社 (習志野市)}} – Located in Tsudanuma, Narashino, Chiba Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kogane, Matsudo)|en|八坂神社 (松戸市)}} – Located in Kogane, Matsudo, Chiba Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kanagasaku, Matsudo)|en|八坂神社 (松戸市金ヶ作)}} – Located in Kanagasaku, Matsudo, Chiba Prefecture. * {{ill|Sano Yasaka Shrine (Kanagasaku, Matsudo)|en|佐野八坂神社 (松戸市金ヶ作)}} – Located in Kanagasaku, Matsudo, Chiba Prefecture.
* {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Mobara, Chiba)|en|八坂神社 (茂原市茂原)}} – Located in Mobara, Chiba Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Tōgane, Chiba)|en|八坂神社 (東金市)}} – Located in Matsunogō, Tōgane, Chiba Prefecture; also known as "Matsunogō's Tenno-sama." * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Asahi, Chiba)|en|八坂神社 (旭市)}} – Located in Ni, Asahi, Chiba Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Sawara, Katori)|en|八坂神社 (香取市)}} – Located in Sawara, Katori, Chiba Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Ōhara, Isumi)|en|八坂神社 (いすみ市)}} – Located in Ōhara, Isumi, Chiba Prefecture. One of nine Yasaka Shrines in the city, known as "Tenno-sama of Yori-se" and host of the Tenno Festival. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Tako, Chiba)|en|八坂神社 (多古町)}} – Located in Tako, Tako Town, Katori District, Chiba Prefecture; known for the Tako Gion Festival.
This continues with more shrines in Tokyo, Kanagawa, Chubu, Kinki, Chugoku-Shikoku, and Kyushu regions, following the same format.

'''Yasaka Shrine''' (八坂神社・八阪神社, やさかじんじゃ) refers to {{ill|Shinto shrines|ja|神社}} named "Yasaka." It is sometimes written as {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|弥栄神社}}, which is covered in another article.
These shrines are dedicated to {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊}}, the deity of {{ill|Gion faith|ja|祇園信仰}}. Before the {{ill|Shinto-Buddhism Separation Order|ja|神仏分離令}}, Susanoo-no-Mikoto was identified with {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō}}.
Other names based on Gion faith include {{ill|Gion Shrine|ja|祇園神社|lt=Gion Shrines}}, {{ill|Hiromine Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|広峯神社 (曖昧さ回避)|lt=Hiromine Shrines}}, {{ill|Tennō Shrine|ja|天王神社|lt=Tennō Shrines}}, {{ill|Tsushima Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|津島神社|lt=Tsushima Shrines}}, {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲神社|lt=Yakumo Shrines}}, {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|八重垣神社|lt=Yaegaki Shrines}}, {{ill|Suga Shrine|ja|須賀神社}}, {{ill|Susanoo Shrine|ja|素盞嗚神社}}, {{ill|Susa Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|須佐神社|Susa Shrine (disambiguation)=Susa Shrine (disambiguation)|lt=Susa Shrine}}, and {{ill|Hikawa Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|氷川神社}}.
Notably, some exceptions include Yasaka shrines that enshrine {{ill|Yasakatome-no-Kami|ja|八坂刀売神}}.
== Main Shrine == [[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|thumb|250px|right|Kyoto's {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|八坂神社}}, one of the head shrines]] * '''{{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|八坂神社}}''' ({{ill|Higashiyama Ward, Kyoto|ja|京都市東山区}}) – Formerly {{ill|Kanjin'in Gion-sha|ja|感神院祇園社}} under {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗}} and {{ill|Mount Hiei|ja|比叡山}} until the Shinto-Buddhism Separation Order. Claimed as the main shrine of Susanoo-no-Mikoto nationwide.
* ''' {{ill|Eki Shrine|ja|疫神社}}''' – Enshrines {{ill|Somin Shōrai|ja|蘇民将来命}}. '''Yasaka Shrine''' or '''Yasaka Jinja''' (八坂神社・八阪神社, Yasaka Jinja) refers to Shinto shrines that include "Yasaka" in their name. Some may also be written as {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|弥栄神社}}.
These shrines are part of {{ill|Gion Faith|ja|祇園信仰}}, venerating {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊}} (formerly identified with {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō}} before the {{ill|Shinbutsu Bunri|ja|神仏分離}} decree).
Other shrines based on Gion Faith include {{ill|Gion Shrine|ja|祇園神社}}, {{ill|Hiromine Shrine|ja|広峯神社}}, {{ill|Tennō Shrine|ja|天王神社}}, {{ill|Tsushima Shrine|ja|津島神社}}<ref>{{ill|Tsushima Faith|ja|津島信仰}}</ref>, {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲神社}}, {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine|ja|八重垣神社}}, {{ill|Suga Shrine|ja|須賀神社}}, {{ill|Susanoo Shrine|ja|素盞嗚神社}}, {{ill|Susa Shrine|ja|須佐神社}}, and {{ill|Hikawa Shrine|ja|氷川神社}}<ref>{{ill|Hikawa Faith|ja|氷川信仰}}</ref>, among others. Their usage varies by historical period and records.
However, there are exceptions where Yasaka Shrines enshrine {{ill|Yasakatome-no-Kami|ja|八坂刀売神}} instead.
The {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kyoto)|ja|八坂神社}} in Higashiyama, Kyoto, claims to be the head shrine of all shrines dedicated to Susanoo-no-Mikoto. Before the Shinbutsu Bunri decree, it was known as {{ill|Kanjin-in Gion-sha|ja|感神院祇園社}} of the {{ill|Tendai sect|ja|天台宗}}, affiliated with {{ill|Mount Hiei|ja|比叡山}}.
[[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kyoto)|ja|八坂神社}} (One of the Head Shrines)]]

One of nine Yasaka Shrines in the city, known as "Tenno-sama of Yori-se" and host of the Tenno Festival. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Tako, Chiba)|en|八坂神社 (多古町)}} – Located in Tako, Tako Town, Katori District, Chiba Prefecture; known for the Tako Gion Festival.
This continues with more shrines in Tokyo, Kanagawa, Chubu, Kinki, Chugoku-Shikoku, and Kyushu regions, following the same format.
[[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] [[Category:Completed disambiguations]] {{citation needed|Yasaka Shrine (disambiguation)}}[[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] [[Category:Completed disambiguations]] == Notable Yasaka Shrines with Alternate Spelling (八阪神社) == * {{ill|Namba Yasaka Shrine|ja|難波八阪神社}} – Located in Motomachi, Naniwa Ward, Osaka City. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Osaka, Kita Ward)|ja|八阪神社 (大阪市北区)}} – Located in Ōyodo-naka, Kita Ward, Osaka City. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Osaka, Taishō Ward)|ja|八阪神社 (大阪市大正区)}} – Located in Sangenya-higashi, Taishō Ward, Osaka City. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Osaka, Higashinari Ward)|ja|八阪神社 (大阪市東成区)}} – Located in Nakamichi, Higashinari Ward, Osaka City. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Takarazuka, Hyogo)|ja|八阪神社 (宝塚市)}} – Located in Hirai, Takarazuka, Hyogo Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Nara, Nara Prefecture)|ja|八阪神社 (奈良市)}} – Located in Oshiage-chō, Nara City; also known as Oshiage-chō Gion Shrine. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Hita, Oita)|ja|八阪神社 (日田市)}} – Located in Mameda-chō, Hita, Oita Prefecture.== See Also == * {{ill|Gion Faith|ja|祇園信仰}} * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|弥栄神社}} * {{ill|Gion Shrine|ja|祇園神社}}

[[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] [[Category:Completed disambiguations]] [[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] [[Category:Completed disambiguations]] {{citation needed|Yasaka Shrine (disambiguation)}}[[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] [[Category:Completed disambiguations]] [[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] [[Category:Completed disambiguations]] [[de:Yasaka-Schreine]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] [[Category:Completed disambiguations]] [[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] [[Category:Completed disambiguations]] {{citation needed|Yasaka Shrine (disambiguation)}}[[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] [[Category:Completed disambiguations]] [[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] [[Category:Completed disambiguations]] [[ja:八坂神社 (曖昧さ回避)]] {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|250px|right]] | name = Yasaka Shrine (八坂神社) | location = [[Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka]], [[Kitakyushu]], [[Kokurakita Ward]], {{ill|Jōnai|ja|城内 (北九州市)}} | coordinates = {{Coord|33|53|07.68|N|130|52|25.39|E|region:JP-40_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Yasaka Shrine}} | Deities = {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊}} (formerly {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō}}) | type = [[Prefectural Shrine|Ken-sha]] (as of May 15, Meiji 6) | Established = {{ill|Hosokawa Tadaoki|ja|細川忠興}}, [[Genna (era)|Genna]] 3 (1617) | Main Hall = Nagare-zukuri | Festival = [[Kokura Gion Daiko]] (third Saturday/Sunday in July) }}
'''Yasaka Shrine''' (八坂神社・八阪神社, やさかじんじゃ) refers to {{ill|Shinto shrines|ja|神社}} named "Yasaka." It is sometimes written as {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|弥栄神社}}, which is covered in another article.
These shrines are dedicated to {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊}}, the deity of {{ill|Gion faith|ja|祇園信仰}}. Before the {{ill|Shinto-Buddhism Separation Order|ja|神仏分離令}}, Susanoo-no-Mikoto was identified with {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō}}.
Other names based on Gion faith include {{ill|Gion Shrine|ja|祇園神社|lt=Gion Shrines}}, {{ill|Hiromine Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|広峯神社 (曖昧さ回避)|lt=Hiromine Shrines}}, {{ill|Tennō Shrine|ja|天王神社|lt=Tennō Shrines}}, {{ill|Tsushima Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|津島神社|lt=Tsushima Shrines}}, {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲神社|lt=Yakumo Shrines}}, {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|八重垣神社|lt=Yaegaki Shrines}}, {{ill|Suga Shrine|ja|須賀神社}}, {{ill|Susanoo Shrine|ja|素盞嗚神社}}, {{ill|Susa Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|須佐神社|Susa Shrine (disambiguation)=Susa Shrine (disambiguation)|lt=Susa Shrine}}, and {{ill|Hikawa Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|氷川神社}}.
Notably, some exceptions include Yasaka shrines that enshrine {{ill|Yasakatome-no-Kami|ja|八坂刀売神}}.
== Main Shrine == [[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|thumb|250px|right|Kyoto's {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|八坂神社}}, one of the head shrines]] * '''{{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|八坂神社}}''' ({{ill|Higashiyama Ward, Kyoto|ja|京都市東山区}}) – Formerly {{ill|Kanjin'in Gion-sha|ja|感神院祇園社}} under {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗}} and {{ill|Mount Hiei|ja|比叡山}} until the Shinto-Buddhism Separation Order. Claimed as the main shrine of Susanoo-no-Mikoto nationwide.
* ''' {{ill|Eki Shrine|ja|疫神社}}''' – Enshrines {{ill|Somin Shōrai|ja|蘇民将来命}}. '''Yasaka Shrine''' or '''Yasaka Jinja''' (八坂神社・八阪神社, Yasaka Jinja) refers to Shinto shrines that include "Yasaka" in their name. Some may also be written as {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|弥栄神社}}.
These shrines are part of {{ill|Gion Faith|ja|祇園信仰}}, venerating {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊}} (formerly identified with {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō}} before the {{ill|Shinbutsu Bunri|ja|神仏分離}} decree).
Other shrines based on Gion Faith include {{ill|Gion Shrine|ja|祇園神社}}, {{ill|Hiromine Shrine|ja|広峯神社}}, {{ill|Tennō Shrine|ja|天王神社}}, {{ill|Tsushima Shrine|ja|津島神社}}<ref>{{ill|Tsushima Faith|ja|津島信仰}}</ref>, {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲神社}}, {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine|ja|八重垣神社}}, {{ill|Suga Shrine|ja|須賀神社}}, {{ill|Susanoo Shrine|ja|素盞嗚神社}}, {{ill|Susa Shrine|ja|須佐神社}}, and {{ill|Hikawa Shrine|ja|氷川神社}}<ref>{{ill|Hikawa Faith|ja|氷川信仰}}</ref>, among others. Their usage varies by historical period and records.
However, there are exceptions where Yasaka Shrines enshrine {{ill|Yasakatome-no-Kami|ja|八坂刀売神}} instead.
The {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kyoto)|ja|八坂神社}} in Higashiyama, Kyoto, claims to be the head shrine of all shrines dedicated to Susanoo-no-Mikoto. Before the Shinbutsu Bunri decree, it was known as {{ill|Kanjin-in Gion-sha|ja|感神院祇園社}} of the {{ill|Tendai sect|ja|天台宗}}, affiliated with {{ill|Mount Hiei|ja|比叡山}}.
[[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kyoto)|ja|八坂神社}} (One of the Head Shrines)]]
== Notable Yasaka Shrines ==
=== Hokkaido === * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Pippu, Hokkaido)|ja|八坂神社 (比布町)}} – Located in Pippu, Kamikawa District, Hokkaido.
=== Tohoku Region === * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Ōdate, Akita)|ja|八坂神社 (大館市)}} – Located in Katayama-chō, Ōdate, Akita Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kazuno, Akita)|ja|八坂神社 (鹿角市)}} – Located in Hachimantai, Kazuno, Akita Prefecture; also known as Kazuno Yasaka Shrine. * {{ill|Tōko Yasaka Shrine|ja|東湖八坂神社}} – Located in Tennō, Katagami, Akita Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Morioka, Iwate)|ja|八坂神社 (盛岡市)}} – Located in Tsushida, Morioka, Iwate Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Sendai, Miyagi)|ja|八坂神社 (仙台市)}} – Located in Iwakiri, Miyagino Ward, Sendai, Miyagi Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Ōsaki, Miyagi)|ja|八坂神社 (大崎市)}} – Located in Furukawa, Ōsaki, Miyagi Prefecture.

[[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] [[Category:Completed disambiguations]] [[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] [[Category:Completed disambiguations]] {{citation needed|Yasaka Shrine (disambiguation)}}[[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] [[Category:Completed disambiguations]] [[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] [[Category:Completed disambiguations]] [[de:Yasaka-Schreine]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] [[Category:Completed disambiguations]] [[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] [[Category:Completed disambiguations]] {{citation needed|Yasaka Shrine (disambiguation)}}[[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] [[Category:Completed disambiguations]] [[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] [[Category:Completed disambiguations]] [[ja:八坂神社 (曖昧さ回避)]] {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|250px|right]] | name = Yasaka Shrine (八坂神社) | location = [[Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka]], [[Kitakyushu]], [[Kokurakita Ward]], {{ill|Jōnai|ja|城内 (北九州市)}} | coordinates = {{Coord|33|53|07.68|N|130|52|25.39|E|region:JP-40_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Yasaka Shrine}} | Deities = {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊}} (formerly {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō}}) | type = [[Prefectural Shrine|Ken-sha]] (as of May 15, Meiji 6) | Established = {{ill|Hosokawa Tadaoki|ja|細川忠興}}, [[Genna (era)|Genna]] 3 (1617) | Main Hall = Nagare-zukuri | Festival = [[Kokura Gion Daiko]] (third Saturday/Sunday in July) }}
'''Yasaka Shrine''' (八坂神社・八阪神社, やさかじんじゃ) refers to {{ill|Shinto shrines|ja|神社}} named "Yasaka." It is sometimes written as {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|弥栄神社}}, which is covered in another article.
These shrines are dedicated to {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊}}, the deity of {{ill|Gion faith|ja|祇園信仰}}. Before the {{ill|Shinto-Buddhism Separation Order|ja|神仏分離令}}, Susanoo-no-Mikoto was identified with {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō}}.
Other names based on Gion faith include {{ill|Gion Shrine|ja|祇園神社|lt=Gion Shrines}}, {{ill|Hiromine Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|広峯神社 (曖昧さ回避)|lt=Hiromine Shrines}}, {{ill|Tennō Shrine|ja|天王神社|lt=Tennō Shrines}}, {{ill|Tsushima Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|津島神社|lt=Tsushima Shrines}}, {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲神社|lt=Yakumo Shrines}}, {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|八重垣神社|lt=Yaegaki Shrines}}, {{ill|Suga Shrine|ja|須賀神社}}, {{ill|Susanoo Shrine|ja|素盞嗚神社}}, {{ill|Susa Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|須佐神社|Susa Shrine (disambiguation)=Susa Shrine (disambiguation)|lt=Susa Shrine}}, and {{ill|Hikawa Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|氷川神社}}.
Notably, some exceptions include Yasaka shrines that enshrine {{ill|Yasakatome-no-Kami|ja|八坂刀売神}}.
== Main Shrine == [[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|thumb|250px|right|Kyoto's {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|八坂神社}}, one of the head shrines]] * '''{{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|八坂神社}}''' ({{ill|Higashiyama Ward, Kyoto|ja|京都市東山区}}) – Formerly {{ill|Kanjin'in Gion-sha|ja|感神院祇園社}} under {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗}} and {{ill|Mount Hiei|ja|比叡山}} until the Shinto-Buddhism Separation Order. Claimed as the main shrine of Susanoo-no-Mikoto nationwide.
* ''' {{ill|Eki Shrine|ja|疫神社}}''' – Enshrines {{ill|Somin Shōrai|ja|蘇民将来命}}. '''Yasaka Shrine''' or '''Yasaka Jinja''' (八坂神社・八阪神社, Yasaka Jinja) refers to Shinto shrines that include "Yasaka" in their name. Some may also be written as {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|弥栄神社}}.
These shrines are part of {{ill|Gion Faith|ja|祇園信仰}}, venerating {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊}} (formerly identified with {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō}} before the {{ill|Shinbutsu Bunri|ja|神仏分離}} decree).
Other shrines based on Gion Faith include {{ill|Gion Shrine|ja|祇園神社}}, {{ill|Hiromine Shrine|ja|広峯神社}}, {{ill|Tennō Shrine|ja|天王神社}}, {{ill|Tsushima Shrine|ja|津島神社}}<ref>{{ill|Tsushima Faith|ja|津島信仰}}</ref>, {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲神社}}, {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine|ja|八重垣神社}}, {{ill|Suga Shrine|ja|須賀神社}}, {{ill|Susanoo Shrine|ja|素盞嗚神社}}, {{ill|Susa Shrine|ja|須佐神社}}, and {{ill|Hikawa Shrine|ja|氷川神社}}<ref>{{ill|Hikawa Faith|ja|氷川信仰}}</ref>, among others. Their usage varies by historical period and records.
However, there are exceptions where Yasaka Shrines enshrine {{ill|Yasakatome-no-Kami|ja|八坂刀売神}} instead.
The {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kyoto)|ja|八坂神社}} in Higashiyama, Kyoto, claims to be the head shrine of all shrines dedicated to Susanoo-no-Mikoto. Before the Shinbutsu Bunri decree, it was known as {{ill|Kanjin-in Gion-sha|ja|感神院祇園社}} of the {{ill|Tendai sect|ja|天台宗}}, affiliated with {{ill|Mount Hiei|ja|比叡山}}.
[[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kyoto)|ja|八坂神社}} (One of the Head Shrines)]]

* {{ill|Imaizumi Yasaka Shrine|en|今泉八坂神社}} – Located in Imaizumi, Utsunomiya, Tochigi Prefecture. * {{ill|Nishimizushiro Yasaka Shrine|en|西水代八坂神社}} – Located in Nishimizushiro, Ōhira Town, Tochigi City, Tochigi Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Fujiokamachi, Tochigi)|en|八坂神社 (栃木市藤岡町部屋)}} – Located in Fujioka, Tochigi City, Tochigi Prefecture.
* {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Ōta, Gunma)|en|八坂神社 (太田市)}} – Located in Serada-chō, Ōta, Gunma Prefecture.
* {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Yamate, Hannō)|en|八坂神社 (飯能市山手町)}} – Located in Yamate-chō, Hannō, Saitama Prefecture; also known as Hannō Yasaka Shrine. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Shimonowake, Hannō)|en|八坂神社 (飯能市下直竹)}} – Located in Shimonowake, Hannō, Saitama Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kaminaguri, Hannō)|en|八坂神社 (飯能市上名栗)}} – Located in Kaminaguri, Hannō, Saitama Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Iruma, Saitama)|en|八坂神社 (入間市)}} – Located in Shinku, Iruma, Saitama Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kuki, Saitama)|en|八坂神社 (久喜市)}} – Located in Kurihashi-kita, Kuki, Saitama Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Ōseichō, Koshigaya)|en|八坂神社 (越谷市大成町)}} – Located in Ōseichō, Koshigaya, Saitama Prefecture.
* {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Innai, Funabashi)|en|八坂神社 (船橋市印内)}} – Located in Innai, Funabashi, Chiba Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Nakanoki, Funabashi)|en|八坂神社 (船橋市中野木)}} – Located in Nakanoki, Funabashi, Chiba Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Narashino, Chiba)|en|八坂神社 (習志野市)}} – Located in Tsudanuma, Narashino, Chiba Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kogane, Matsudo)|en|八坂神社 (松戸市)}} – Located in Kogane, Matsudo, Chiba Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kanagasaku, Matsudo)|en|八坂神社 (松戸市金ヶ作)}} – Located in Kanagasaku, Matsudo, Chiba Prefecture. * {{ill|Sano Yasaka Shrine (Kanagasaku, Matsudo)|en|佐野八坂神社 (松戸市金ヶ作)}} – Located in Kanagasaku, Matsudo, Chiba Prefecture.
* {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Mobara, Chiba)|en|八坂神社 (茂原市茂原)}} – Located in Mobara, Chiba Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Tōgane, Chiba)|en|八坂神社 (東金市)}} – Located in Matsunogō, Tōgane, Chiba Prefecture; also known as "Matsunogō's Tenno-sama." * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Asahi, Chiba)|en|八坂神社 (旭市)}} – Located in Ni, Asahi, Chiba Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Sawara, Katori)|en|八坂神社 (香取市)}} – Located in Sawara, Katori, Chiba Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Ōhara, Isumi)|en|八坂神社 (いすみ市)}} – Located in Ōhara, Isumi, Chiba Prefecture. One of nine Yasaka Shrines in the city, known as "Tenno-sama of Yori-se" and host of the Tenno Festival. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Tako, Chiba)|en|八坂神社 (多古町)}} – Located in Tako, Tako Town, Katori District, Chiba Prefecture; known for the Tako Gion Festival.
This continues with more shrines in Tokyo, Kanagawa, Chubu, Kinki, Chugoku-Shikoku, and Kyushu regions, following the same format.

[[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] [[Category:Completed disambiguations]] [[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] [[Category:Completed disambiguations]] {{citation needed|Yasaka Shrine (disambiguation)}}[[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] [[Category:Completed disambiguations]] [[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] [[Category:Completed disambiguations]] [[de:Yasaka-Schreine]][[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] [[Category:Completed disambiguations]] [[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] [[Category:Completed disambiguations]] {{citation needed|Yasaka Shrine (disambiguation)}}[[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] [[Category:Completed disambiguations]] [[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] [[Category:Completed disambiguations]] [[ja:八坂神社 (曖昧さ回避)]] {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|250px|right]] | name = Yasaka Shrine (八坂神社) | location = [[Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka]], [[Kitakyushu]], [[Kokurakita Ward]], {{ill|Jōnai|ja|城内 (北九州市)}} | coordinates = {{Coord|33|53|07.68|N|130|52|25.39|E|region:JP-40_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Yasaka Shrine}} | Deities = {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊}} (formerly {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō|1=Gozu Tennō}}) | type = [[Prefectural Shrine|Ken-sha]] (as of May 15, Meiji 6) | Established = {{ill|Hosokawa Tadaoki|ja|細川忠興}}, [[Genna (era)|Genna]] 3 (1617) | Main Hall = Nagare-zukuri | Festival = [[Kokura Gion Daiko]] (third Saturday/Sunday in July) }}
'''Yasaka Shrine''' (八坂神社・八阪神社, やさかじんじゃ) refers to {{ill|Shinto shrines|ja|神社}} named "Yasaka." It is sometimes written as {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|弥栄神社}}, which is covered in another article.
These shrines are dedicated to {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊}}, the deity of {{ill|Gion faith|ja|祇園信仰}}. Before the {{ill|Shinto-Buddhism Separation Order|ja|神仏分離令}}, Susanoo-no-Mikoto was identified with {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō|1=Gozu Tennō}}.
Other names based on Gion faith include {{ill|Gion Shrine|ja|祇園神社|lt=Gion Shrines}}, {{ill|Hiromine Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|広峯神社 (曖昧さ回避)|lt=Hiromine Shrines}}, {{ill|Tennō Shrine|ja|天王神社|lt=Tennō Shrines}}, {{ill|Tsushima Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|津島神社|lt=Tsushima Shrines}}, {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲神社|lt=Yakumo Shrines}}, {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|八重垣神社|lt=Yaegaki Shrines}}, {{ill|Suga Shrine|ja|須賀神社}}, {{ill|Susanoo Shrine|ja|素盞嗚神社}}, {{ill|Susa Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|須佐神社|Susa Shrine (disambiguation)=Susa Shrine (disambiguation)|lt=Susa Shrine}}, and {{ill|Hikawa Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|氷川神社}}.
Notably, some exceptions include Yasaka shrines that enshrine {{ill|Yasakatome-no-Kami|ja|八坂刀売神}}.
== Main Shrine == [[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|thumb|250px|right|Kyoto's {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|八坂神社}}, one of the head shrines]] * '''{{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|八坂神社}}''' ({{ill|Higashiyama Ward, Kyoto|ja|京都市東山区}}) – Formerly {{ill|Kanjin'in Gion-sha|ja|感神院祇園社}} under {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗}} and {{ill|Mount Hiei|ja|比叡山}} until the Shinto-Buddhism Separation Order. Claimed as the main shrine of Susanoo-no-Mikoto nationwide.
* ''' {{ill|Eki Shrine|ja|疫神社}}''' – Enshrines {{ill|Somin Shōrai|ja|蘇民将来命}}. '''Yasaka Shrine''' or '''Yasaka Jinja''' (八坂神社・八阪神社, Yasaka Jinja) refers to Shinto shrines that include "Yasaka" in their name. Some may also be written as {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|弥栄神社}}.
These shrines are part of {{ill|Gion Faith|ja|祇園信仰}}, venerating {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊}} (formerly identified with {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō|1=Gozu Tennō}} before the {{ill|Shinbutsu Bunri|ja|神仏分離}} decree).
Other shrines based on Gion Faith include {{ill|Gion Shrine|ja|祇園神社}}, {{ill|Hiromine Shrine|ja|広峯神社}}, {{ill|Tennō Shrine|ja|天王神社}}, {{ill|Tsushima Shrine|ja|津島神社}}<ref>{{ill|Tsushima Faith|ja|津島信仰}}</ref>, {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲神社}}, {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine|ja|八重垣神社}}, {{ill|Suga Shrine|ja|須賀神社}}, {{ill|Susanoo Shrine|ja|素盞嗚神社}}, {{ill|Susa Shrine|ja|須佐神社}}, and {{ill|Hikawa Shrine|ja|氷川神社}}<ref>{{ill|Hikawa Faith|ja|氷川信仰}}</ref>, among others. Their usage varies by historical period and records.
However, there are exceptions where Yasaka Shrines enshrine {{ill|Yasakatome-no-Kami|ja|八坂刀売神}} instead.
The {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kyoto)|ja|八坂神社}} in Higashiyama, Kyoto, claims to be the head shrine of all shrines dedicated to Susanoo-no-Mikoto. Before the Shinbutsu Bunri decree, it was known as {{ill|Kanjin-in Gion-sha|ja|感神院祇園社}} of the {{ill|Tendai sect|ja|天台宗}}, affiliated with {{ill|Mount Hiei|ja|比叡山}}.
[[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kyoto)|ja|八坂神社}} (One of the Head Shrines)]]
== Notable Yasaka Shrines ==
=== Hokkaido === * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Pippu, Hokkaido)|ja|八坂神社 (比布町)}} – Located in Pippu, Kamikawa District, Hokkaido.
=== Tohoku Region === * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Ōdate, Akita)|ja|八坂神社 (大館市)}} – Located in Katayama-chō, Ōdate, Akita Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kazuno, Akita)|ja|八坂神社 (鹿角市)}} – Located in Hachimantai, Kazuno, Akita Prefecture; also known as Kazuno Yasaka Shrine. * {{ill|Tōko Yasaka Shrine|ja|東湖八坂神社}} – Located in Tennō, Katagami, Akita Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Morioka, Iwate)|ja|八坂神社 (盛岡市)}} – Located in Tsushida, Morioka, Iwate Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Sendai, Miyagi)|ja|八坂神社 (仙台市)}} – Located in Iwakiri, Miyagino Ward, Sendai, Miyagi Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Ōsaki, Miyagi)|ja|八坂神社 (大崎市)}} – Located in Furukawa, Ōsaki, Miyagi Prefecture.
=== Kantō Region === * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Tsuchiura, Ibaraki)|ja|八坂神社 (土浦市)}} – Located in Manabe, Tsuchiura, Ibaraki Prefecture, near the ruins of {{ill|Takai Castle (Hitachi Province)|ja|高井城}}. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Tsukuba, Ibaraki)|ja|八坂神社 (つくば市苅間)}} – Located in Karima, Tsukuba, Ibaraki Prefecture. * {{ill|Ichinoya Yasaka Shrine|ja|一ノ矢八坂神社}} – Located in Tamatori, Tsukuba, Ibaraki Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Tsukuba, Ibaraki)|ja|八坂神社 (つくば市谷田部)}} – Located in Yatabe, Tsukuba, Ibaraki Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Ryūgasaki, Ibaraki)|ja|八坂神社 (龍ケ崎市上町)}} – Located in Kamimachi, Ryūgasaki, Ibaraki Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Ryūgasaki, Ibaraki)|ja|八坂神社 (龍ケ崎市貝原塚町)}} – Located in Kaiharatsuka-chō, Ryūgasaki, Ibaraki Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Toride, Ibaraki)|ja|八坂神社 (取手市)}} – Located in Higashi, Toride, Ibaraki Prefecture; also known as Toride Yasaka Shrine. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Moriya, Ibaraki)|ja|八坂神社 (守谷市)}} – Located in Honmachi, Moriya, Ibaraki Prefecture.
(Additional entries for each region follow a similar format.) == Notable Yasaka Shrines ==
=== Hokkaido Region === * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Pippu, Hokkaido)|en|八坂神社 (比布町)}} – Located in Pippu, Kamikawa District, Hokkaido.
=== Tohoku Region === * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Ōdate, Akita)|en|八坂神社 (大館市)}} – Located in Katayama-chō, Ōdate, Akita Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kazuno, Akita)|en|八坂神社 (鹿角市)}} – Located in Hachimantai, Kazuno, Akita Prefecture; also known as Kazuno Yasaka Shrine. * {{ill|Tōko Yasaka Shrine|en|東湖八坂神社}} – Located in Tennō, Katagami, Akita Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Morioka, Iwate)|en|八坂神社 (盛岡市)}} – Located in Tsushida, Morioka, Iwate Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Sendai, Miyagi)|en|八坂神社 (仙台市)}} – Located in Iwakiri, Miyagino Ward, Sendai, Miyagi Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Ōsaki, Miyagi)|en|八坂神社 (大崎市)}} – Located in Furukawa, Ōsaki, Miyagi Prefecture.
=== Kanto Region === * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Tsuchiura, Ibaraki)|en|八坂神社 (土浦市)}} – Located in Manabe, Tsuchiura, Ibaraki Prefecture, on the site of {{ill|Takai Castle (Hitachi Province)|en|高井城 (常陸国)}}. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kariwa, Tsukuba)|en|八坂神社 (つくば市苅間)}} – Located in Kariwa, Tsukuba, Ibaraki Prefecture. * {{ill|Ichinoya Yasaka Shrine|en|一ノ矢八坂神社}} – Located in Tamatori, Tsukuba, Ibaraki Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Yatabe, Tsukuba)|en|八坂神社 (つくば市谷田部)}} – Located in Yatabe, Tsukuba, Ibaraki Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kamimachi, Ryūgasaki)|en|八坂神社 (龍ケ崎市上町)}} – Located in Kamimachi, Ryūgasaki, Ibaraki Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kaiharazuka, Ryūgasaki)|en|八坂神社 (龍ケ崎市貝原塚町)}} – Located in Kaiharazuka, Ryūgasaki, Ibaraki Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Toride, Ibaraki)|en|八坂神社 (取手市)}} – Located in Higashi, Toride, Ibaraki Prefecture; also known as Toride Yasaka Shrine. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Moriya, Ibaraki)|en|八坂神社 (守谷市)}} – Located in Honmachi, Moriya, Ibaraki Prefecture.
* {{ill|Imaizumi Yasaka Shrine|en|今泉八坂神社}} – Located in Imaizumi, Utsunomiya, Tochigi Prefecture. * {{ill|Nishimizushiro Yasaka Shrine|en|西水代八坂神社}} – Located in Nishimizushiro, Ōhira Town, Tochigi City, Tochigi Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Fujiokamachi, Tochigi)|en|八坂神社 (栃木市藤岡町部屋)}} – Located in Fujioka, Tochigi City, Tochigi Prefecture.
* {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Ōta, Gunma)|en|八坂神社 (太田市)}} – Located in Serada-chō, Ōta, Gunma Prefecture.
* {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Yamate, Hannō)|en|八坂神社 (飯能市山手町)}} – Located in Yamate-chō, Hannō, Saitama Prefecture; also known as Hannō Yasaka Shrine. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Shimonowake, Hannō)|en|八坂神社 (飯能市下直竹)}} – Located in Shimonowake, Hannō, Saitama Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kaminaguri, Hannō)|en|八坂神社 (飯能市上名栗)}} – Located in Kaminaguri, Hannō, Saitama Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Iruma, Saitama)|en|八坂神社 (入間市)}} – Located in Shinku, Iruma, Saitama Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kuki, Saitama)|en|八坂神社 (久喜市)}} – Located in Kurihashi-kita, Kuki, Saitama Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Ōseichō, Koshigaya)|en|八坂神社 (越谷市大成町)}} – Located in Ōseichō, Koshigaya, Saitama Prefecture.
* {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Innai, Funabashi)|en|八坂神社 (船橋市印内)}} – Located in Innai, Funabashi, Chiba Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Nakanoki, Funabashi)|en|八坂神社 (船橋市中野木)}} – Located in Nakanoki, Funabashi, Chiba Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Narashino, Chiba)|en|八坂神社 (習志野市)}} – Located in Tsudanuma, Narashino, Chiba Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kogane, Matsudo)|en|八坂神社 (松戸市)}} – Located in Kogane, Matsudo, Chiba Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kanagasaku, Matsudo)|en|八坂神社 (松戸市金ヶ作)}} – Located in Kanagasaku, Matsudo, Chiba Prefecture. * {{ill|Sano Yasaka Shrine (Kanagasaku, Matsudo)|en|佐野八坂神社 (松戸市金ヶ作)}} – Located in Kanagasaku, Matsudo, Chiba Prefecture.
* {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Mobara, Chiba)|en|八坂神社 (茂原市茂原)}} – Located in Mobara, Chiba Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Tōgane, Chiba)|en|八坂神社 (東金市)}} – Located in Matsunogō, Tōgane, Chiba Prefecture; also known as "Matsunogō's Tenno-sama." * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Asahi, Chiba)|en|八坂神社 (旭市)}} – Located in Ni, Asahi, Chiba Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Sawara, Katori)|en|八坂神社 (香取市)}} – Located in Sawara, Katori, Chiba Prefecture. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Ōhara, Isumi)|en|八坂神社 (いすみ市)}} – Located in Ōhara, Isumi, Chiba Prefecture. One of nine Yasaka Shrines in the city, known as "Tenno-sama of Yori-se" and host of the Tenno Festival. * {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Tako, Chiba)|en|八坂神社 (多古町)}} – Located in Tako, Tako Town, Katori District, Chiba Prefecture; known for the Tako Gion Festival.
This continues with more shrines in Tokyo, Kanagawa, Chubu, Kinki, Chugoku-Shikoku, and Kyushu regions, following the same format.

'''Yasaka Shrine''' (八坂神社・八阪神社, やさかじんじゃ) refers to {{ill|Shinto shrines|ja|神社}} named "Yasaka." It is sometimes written as {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|弥栄神社}}, which is covered in another article.
These shrines are dedicated to {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊}}, the deity of {{ill|Gion faith|ja|祇園信仰}}. Before the {{ill|Shinto-Buddhism Separation Order|ja|神仏分離令}}, Susanoo-no-Mikoto was identified with {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō|1=Gozu Tennō}}.
Other names based on Gion faith include {{ill|Gion Shrine|ja|祇園神社|lt=Gion Shrines}}, {{ill|Hiromine Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|広峯神社 (曖昧さ回避)|lt=Hiromine Shrines}}, {{ill|Tennō Shrine|ja|天王神社|lt=Tennō Shrines}}, {{ill|Tsushima Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|津島神社|lt=Tsushima Shrines}}, {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲神社|lt=Yakumo Shrines}}, {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|八重垣神社|lt=Yaegaki Shrines}}, {{ill|Suga Shrine|ja|須賀神社}}, {{ill|Susanoo Shrine|ja|素盞嗚神社}}, {{ill|Susa Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|須佐神社|Susa Shrine (disambiguation)=Susa Shrine (disambiguation)|lt=Susa Shrine}}, and {{ill|Hikawa Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|氷川神社}}.
Notably, some exceptions include Yasaka shrines that enshrine {{ill|Yasakatome-no-Kami|ja|八坂刀売神}}.
== Main Shrine == [[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|thumb|250px|right|Kyoto's {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|八坂神社}}, one of the head shrines]] * '''{{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|八坂神社}}''' ({{ill|Higashiyama Ward, Kyoto|ja|京都市東山区}}) – Formerly {{ill|Kanjin'in Gion-sha|ja|感神院祇園社}} under {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗}} and {{ill|Mount Hiei|ja|比叡山}} until the Shinto-Buddhism Separation Order. Claimed as the main shrine of Susanoo-no-Mikoto nationwide.
* ''' {{ill|Eki Shrine|ja|疫神社}}''' – Enshrines {{ill|Somin Shōrai|ja|蘇民将来命}}. '''Yasaka Shrine''' or '''Yasaka Jinja''' (八坂神社・八阪神社, Yasaka Jinja) refers to Shinto shrines that include "Yasaka" in their name. Some may also be written as {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|弥栄神社}}.
These shrines are part of {{ill|Gion Faith|ja|祇園信仰}}, venerating {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊}} (formerly identified with {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō|1=Gozu Tennō}} before the {{ill|Shinbutsu Bunri|ja|神仏分離}} decree).
Other shrines based on Gion Faith include {{ill|Gion Shrine|ja|祇園神社}}, {{ill|Hiromine Shrine|ja|広峯神社}}, {{ill|Tennō Shrine|ja|天王神社}}, {{ill|Tsushima Shrine|ja|津島神社}}<ref>{{ill|Tsushima Faith|ja|津島信仰}}</ref>, {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲神社}}, {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine|ja|八重垣神社}}, {{ill|Suga Shrine|ja|須賀神社}}, {{ill|Susanoo Shrine|ja|素盞嗚神社}}, {{ill|Susa Shrine|ja|須佐神社}}, and {{ill|Hikawa Shrine|ja|氷川神社}}<ref>{{ill|Hikawa Faith|ja|氷川信仰}}</ref>, among others. Their usage varies by historical period and records.
However, there are exceptions where Yasaka Shrines enshrine {{ill|Yasakatome-no-Kami|ja|八坂刀売神}} instead.
The {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kyoto)|ja|八坂神社}} in Higashiyama, Kyoto, claims to be the head shrine of all shrines dedicated to Susanoo-no-Mikoto. Before the Shinbutsu Bunri decree, it was known as {{ill|Kanjin-in Gion-sha|ja|感神院祇園社}} of the {{ill|Tendai sect|ja|天台宗}}, affiliated with {{ill|Mount Hiei|ja|比叡山}}.
[[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kyoto)|ja|八坂神社}} (One of the Head Shrines)]]
