'''Yasaka Shrine''' (八坂神社・八阪神社, やさかじんじゃ) refers to {{ill|Shinto shrines|ja|神社|12=draft}} named "Yasaka." It is sometimes written as {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|弥栄神社|12=draft}}, which is covered in another article.
These shrines are dedicated to {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊|12=draft}}, the deity of {{ill|Gion faith|ja|祇園信仰|12=draft}}. Before the {{ill|Shinto-Buddhism Separation Order|ja|神仏分離令|12=draft}}, Susanoo-no-Mikoto was identified with {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō|1=Gozu Tennō|12=draft}}.
Other names based on Gion faith include {{ill|Gion Shrine|ja|祇園神社|lt=Gion Shrines|12=draft}}, {{ill|Hiromine Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|広峯神社 (曖昧さ回避)|lt=Hiromine Shrines|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tennō Shrine|ja|天王神社|lt=Tennō Shrines|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tsushima Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|津島神社|lt=Tsushima Shrines|12=draft}}, {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲神社|lt=Yakumo Shrines|12=draft}}, {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|八重垣神社|lt=Yaegaki Shrines|12=draft}}, {{ill|Suga Shrine|ja|須賀神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Susanoo Shrine|ja|素盞嗚神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Susa Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|須佐神社|Susa Shrine (disambiguation)=Susa Shrine (disambiguation)|lt=Susa Shrine|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Hikawa Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|氷川神社|12=draft}}.
Notably, some exceptions include Yasaka shrines that enshrine {{ill|Yasakatome-no-Kami|ja|八坂刀売神|12=draft}}.
== Main Shrine == [[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|thumb|250px|right|Kyoto's {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|八坂神社|12=draft}}, one of the head shrines]] * '''{{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|八坂神社|12=draft}}''' ({{ill|Higashiyama Ward, Kyoto|ja|京都市東山区|12=draft}}) – Formerly {{ill|Kanjin'in Gion-sha|ja|感神院祇園社|12=draft}} under {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗|12=draft}} and {{ill|Mount Hiei|ja|比叡山|12=draft}} until the Shinto-Buddhism Separation Order. Claimed as the main shrine of Susanoo-no-Mikoto nationwide.
* ''' {{ill|Eki Shrine|ja|疫神社|12=draft}}''' – Enshrines {{ill|Somin Shōrai|ja|蘇民将来命|12=draft}}. '''Yasaka Shrine''' or '''Yasaka Jinja''' (八坂神社・八阪神社, Yasaka Jinja) refers to Shinto shrines that include "Yasaka" in their name. Some may also be written as {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|弥栄神社|12=draft}}.
These shrines are part of {{ill|Gion Faith|ja|祇園信仰|12=draft}}, venerating {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊|12=draft}} (formerly identified with {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō|1=Gozu Tennō|12=draft}} before the {{ill|Shinbutsu Bunri|ja|神仏分離|12=draft}} decree).
Other shrines based on Gion Faith include {{ill|Gion Shrine|ja|祇園神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Hiromine Shrine|ja|広峯神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tennō Shrine|ja|天王神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tsushima Shrine|ja|津島神社|12=draft}}<ref>{{ill|Tsushima Faith|ja|津島信仰|12=draft}}</ref>, {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine|ja|八重垣神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Suga Shrine|ja|須賀神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Susanoo Shrine|ja|素盞嗚神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Susa Shrine|ja|須佐神社|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Hikawa Shrine|ja|氷川神社|12=draft}}<ref>{{ill|Hikawa Faith|ja|氷川信仰|12=draft}}</ref>, among others. Their usage varies by historical period and records.
However, there are exceptions where Yasaka Shrines enshrine {{ill|Yasakatome-no-Kami|ja|八坂刀売神|12=draft}} instead.
The {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kyoto)|ja|八坂神社|12=draft}} in Higashiyama, Kyoto, claims to be the head shrine of all shrines dedicated to Susanoo-no-Mikoto. Before the Shinbutsu Bunri decree, it was known as {{ill|Kanjin-in Gion-sha|ja|感神院祇園社|12=draft}} of the {{ill|Tendai sect|ja|天台宗|12=draft}}, affiliated with {{ill|Mount Hiei|ja|比叡山|12=draft}}.

'''Yasaka Shrine''' (八坂神社・八阪神社, やさかじんじゃ) refers to {{ill|Shinto shrines|ja|神社|12=draft}} named "Yasaka." It is sometimes written as {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|弥栄神社|12=draft}}, which is covered in another article.
These shrines are dedicated to {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊|12=draft}}, the deity of {{ill|Gion faith|ja|祇園信仰|12=draft}}. Before the {{ill|Shinto-Buddhism Separation Order|ja|神仏分離令|12=draft}}, Susanoo-no-Mikoto was identified with {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō|1=Gozu Tennō|12=draft}}.
Other names based on Gion faith include {{ill|Gion Shrine|ja|祇園神社|lt=Gion Shrines|12=draft}}, {{ill|Hiromine Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|広峯神社 (曖昧さ回避)|lt=Hiromine Shrines|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tennō Shrine|ja|天王神社|lt=Tennō Shrines|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tsushima Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|津島神社|lt=Tsushima Shrines|12=draft}}, {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲神社|lt=Yakumo Shrines|12=draft}}, {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|八重垣神社|lt=Yaegaki Shrines|12=draft}}, {{ill|Suga Shrine|ja|須賀神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Susanoo Shrine|ja|素盞嗚神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Susa Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|須佐神社|Susa Shrine (disambiguation)=Susa Shrine (disambiguation)|lt=Susa Shrine|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Hikawa Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|氷川神社|12=draft}}.
Notably, some exceptions include Yasaka shrines that enshrine {{ill|Yasakatome-no-Kami|ja|八坂刀売神|12=draft}}.
== Main Shrine == [[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|thumb|250px|right|Kyoto's {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|八坂神社|12=draft}}, one of the head shrines]] * '''{{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|八坂神社|12=draft}}''' ({{ill|Higashiyama Ward, Kyoto|ja|京都市東山区|12=draft}}) – Formerly {{ill|Kanjin'in Gion-sha|ja|感神院祇園社|12=draft}} under {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗|12=draft}} and {{ill|Mount Hiei|ja|比叡山|12=draft}} until the Shinto-Buddhism Separation Order. Claimed as the main shrine of Susanoo-no-Mikoto nationwide.
* ''' {{ill|Eki Shrine|ja|疫神社|12=draft}}''' – Enshrines {{ill|Somin Shōrai|ja|蘇民将来命|12=draft}}. '''Yasaka Shrine''' or '''Yasaka Jinja''' (八坂神社・八阪神社, Yasaka Jinja) refers to Shinto shrines that include "Yasaka" in their name. Some may also be written as {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|弥栄神社|12=draft}}.
These shrines are part of {{ill|Gion Faith|ja|祇園信仰|12=draft}}, venerating {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊|12=draft}} (formerly identified with {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō|1=Gozu Tennō|12=draft}} before the {{ill|Shinbutsu Bunri|ja|神仏分離|12=draft}} decree).
Other shrines based on Gion Faith include {{ill|Gion Shrine|ja|祇園神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Hiromine Shrine|ja|広峯神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tennō Shrine|ja|天王神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tsushima Shrine|ja|津島神社|12=draft}}<ref>{{ill|Tsushima Faith|ja|津島信仰|12=draft}}</ref>, {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine|ja|八重垣神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Suga Shrine|ja|須賀神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Susanoo Shrine|ja|素盞嗚神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Susa Shrine|ja|須佐神社|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Hikawa Shrine|ja|氷川神社|12=draft}}<ref>{{ill|Hikawa Faith|ja|氷川信仰|12=draft}}</ref>, among others. Their usage varies by historical period and records.
However, there are exceptions where Yasaka Shrines enshrine {{ill|Yasakatome-no-Kami|ja|八坂刀売神|12=draft}} instead.
The {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kyoto)|ja|八坂神社|12=draft}} in Higashiyama, Kyoto, claims to be the head shrine of all shrines dedicated to Susanoo-no-Mikoto. Before the Shinbutsu Bunri decree, it was known as {{ill|Kanjin-in Gion-sha|ja|感神院祇園社|12=draft}} of the {{ill|Tendai sect|ja|天台宗|12=draft}}, affiliated with {{ill|Mount Hiei|ja|比叡山|12=draft}}.

== Main Shrine == [[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|thumb|250px|right|Kyoto's {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|八坂神社|12=draft}}, one of the head shrines]] * '''{{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|八坂神社|12=draft}}''' ({{ill|Higashiyama Ward, Kyoto|ja|京都市東山区|12=draft}}) – Formerly {{ill|Kanjin'in Gion-sha|ja|感神院祇園社|12=draft}} under {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗|12=draft}} and {{ill|Mount Hiei|ja|比叡山|12=draft}} until the Shinto-Buddhism Separation Order. Claimed as the main shrine of Susanoo-no-Mikoto nationwide.
* ''' {{ill|Eki Shrine|ja|疫神社|12=draft}}''' – Enshrines {{ill|Somin Shōrai|ja|蘇民将来命|12=draft}}. '''Yasaka Shrine''' or '''Yasaka Jinja''' (八坂神社・八阪神社, Yasaka Jinja) refers to Shinto shrines that include "Yasaka" in their name. Some may also be written as {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|弥栄神社|12=draft}}.
These shrines are part of {{ill|Gion Faith|ja|祇園信仰|12=draft}}, venerating {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊|12=draft}} (formerly identified with {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō|1=Gozu Tennō|12=draft}} before the {{ill|Shinbutsu Bunri|ja|神仏分離|12=draft}} decree).
Other shrines based on Gion Faith include {{ill|Gion Shrine|ja|祇園神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Hiromine Shrine|ja|広峯神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tennō Shrine|ja|天王神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tsushima Shrine|ja|津島神社|12=draft}}<ref>{{ill|Tsushima Faith|ja|津島信仰|12=draft}}</ref>, {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine|ja|八重垣神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Suga Shrine|ja|須賀神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Susanoo Shrine|ja|素盞嗚神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Susa Shrine|ja|須佐神社|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Hikawa Shrine|ja|氷川神社|12=draft}}<ref>{{ill|Hikawa Faith|ja|氷川信仰|12=draft}}</ref>, among others. Their usage varies by historical period and records.
However, there are exceptions where Yasaka Shrines enshrine {{ill|Yasakatome-no-Kami|ja|八坂刀売神|12=draft}} instead.
The {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kyoto)|ja|八坂神社|12=draft}} in Higashiyama, Kyoto, claims to be the head shrine of all shrines dedicated to Susanoo-no-Mikoto. Before the Shinbutsu Bunri decree, it was known as {{ill|Kanjin-in Gion-sha|ja|感神院祇園社|12=draft}} of the {{ill|Tendai sect|ja|天台宗|12=draft}}, affiliated with {{ill|Mount Hiei|ja|比叡山|12=draft}}.

Their usage varies by historical period and records.
However, there are exceptions where Yasaka Shrines enshrine {{ill|Yasakatome-no-Kami|ja|八坂刀売神|12=draft}} instead.
The {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kyoto)|ja|八坂神社|12=draft}} in Higashiyama, Kyoto, claims to be the head shrine of all shrines dedicated to Susanoo-no-Mikoto. Before the Shinbutsu Bunri decree, it was known as {{ill|Kanjin-in Gion-sha|ja|感神院祇園社|12=draft}} of the {{ill|Tendai sect|ja|天台宗|12=draft}}, affiliated with {{ill|Mount Hiei|ja|比叡山|12=draft}}.

{{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|250px|right]] | name = Yasaka Shrine (八坂神社) | location = [[Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka]], [[Kitakyushu]], [[Kokurakita Ward]], {{ill|Jōnai|ja|城内 (北九州市)|12=draft}} | coordinates = {{Coord|33|53|07.68|N|130|52|25.39|E|region:JP-40_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Yasaka Shrine}} | Deities = {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊|12=draft}} (formerly {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō|1=Gozu Tennō|12=draft}}) | type = [[Prefectural Shrine|Ken-sha]] (as of May 15, Meiji 6) | Established = {{ill|Hosokawa Tadaoki|ja|細川忠興|12=draft}}, [[Genna (era)|Genna]] 3 (1617) | Main Hall = Nagare-zukuri | Festival = [[Kokura Gion Daiko]] (third Saturday/Sunday in July) }}
'''Yasaka Shrine''' (八坂神社・八阪神社, やさかじんじゃ) refers to {{ill|Shinto shrines|ja|神社|12=draft}} named "Yasaka." It is sometimes written as {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|弥栄神社|12=draft}}, which is covered in another article.
These shrines are dedicated to {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊|12=draft}}, the deity of {{ill|Gion faith|ja|祇園信仰|12=draft}}. Before the {{ill|Shinto-Buddhism Separation Order|ja|神仏分離令|12=draft}}, Susanoo-no-Mikoto was identified with {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō|1=Gozu Tennō|12=draft}}.
Other names based on Gion faith include {{ill|Gion Shrine|ja|祇園神社|lt=Gion Shrines|12=draft}}, {{ill|Hiromine Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|広峯神社 (曖昧さ回避)|lt=Hiromine Shrines|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tennō Shrine|ja|天王神社|lt=Tennō Shrines|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tsushima Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|津島神社|lt=Tsushima Shrines|12=draft}}, {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲神社|lt=Yakumo Shrines|12=draft}}, {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|八重垣神社|lt=Yaegaki Shrines|12=draft}}, {{ill|Suga Shrine|ja|須賀神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Susanoo Shrine|ja|素盞嗚神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Susa Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|須佐神社|Susa Shrine (disambiguation)=Susa Shrine (disambiguation)|lt=Susa Shrine|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Hikawa Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|氷川神社|12=draft}}.
Notably, some exceptions include Yasaka shrines that enshrine {{ill|Yasakatome-no-Kami|ja|八坂刀売神|12=draft}}.
== Main Shrine == [[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|thumb|250px|right|Kyoto's {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|八坂神社|12=draft}}, one of the head shrines]] * '''{{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|八坂神社|12=draft}}''' ({{ill|Higashiyama Ward, Kyoto|ja|京都市東山区|12=draft}}) – Formerly {{ill|Kanjin'in Gion-sha|ja|感神院祇園社|12=draft}} under {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗|12=draft}} and {{ill|Mount Hiei|ja|比叡山|12=draft}} until the Shinto-Buddhism Separation Order. Claimed as the main shrine of Susanoo-no-Mikoto nationwide.
* ''' {{ill|Eki Shrine|ja|疫神社|12=draft}}''' – Enshrines {{ill|Somin Shōrai|ja|蘇民将来命|12=draft}}. '''Yasaka Shrine''' or '''Yasaka Jinja''' (八坂神社・八阪神社, Yasaka Jinja) refers to Shinto shrines that include "Yasaka" in their name. Some may also be written as {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|弥栄神社|12=draft}}.
These shrines are part of {{ill|Gion Faith|ja|祇園信仰|12=draft}}, venerating {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊|12=draft}} (formerly identified with {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō|1=Gozu Tennō|12=draft}} before the {{ill|Shinbutsu Bunri|ja|神仏分離|12=draft}} decree).
Other shrines based on Gion Faith include {{ill|Gion Shrine|ja|祇園神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Hiromine Shrine|ja|広峯神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tennō Shrine|ja|天王神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tsushima Shrine|ja|津島神社|12=draft}}<ref>{{ill|Tsushima Faith|ja|津島信仰|12=draft}}</ref>, {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine|ja|八重垣神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Suga Shrine|ja|須賀神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Susanoo Shrine|ja|素盞嗚神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Susa Shrine|ja|須佐神社|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Hikawa Shrine|ja|氷川神社|12=draft}}<ref>{{ill|Hikawa Faith|ja|氷川信仰|12=draft}}</ref>, among others. Their usage varies by historical period and records.
However, there are exceptions where Yasaka Shrines enshrine {{ill|Yasakatome-no-Kami|ja|八坂刀売神|12=draft}} instead.
The {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kyoto)|ja|八坂神社|12=draft}} in Higashiyama, Kyoto, claims to be the head shrine of all shrines dedicated to Susanoo-no-Mikoto. Before the Shinbutsu Bunri decree, it was known as {{ill|Kanjin-in Gion-sha|ja|感神院祇園社|12=draft}} of the {{ill|Tendai sect|ja|天台宗|12=draft}}, affiliated with {{ill|Mount Hiei|ja|比叡山|12=draft}}.

{{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|250px|right]] | name = Yasaka Shrine (八坂神社) | location = [[Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka]], [[Kitakyushu]], [[Kokurakita Ward]], {{ill|Jōnai|ja|城内 (北九州市)|12=draft}} | coordinates = {{Coord|33|53|07.68|N|130|52|25.39|E|region:JP-40_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Yasaka Shrine}} | Deities = {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊|12=draft}} (formerly {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō|1=Gozu Tennō|12=draft}}) | type = [[Prefectural Shrine|Ken-sha]] (as of May 15, Meiji 6) | Established = {{ill|Hosokawa Tadaoki|ja|細川忠興|12=draft}}, [[Genna (era)|Genna]] 3 (1617) | Main Hall = Nagare-zukuri | Festival = [[Kokura Gion Daiko]] (third Saturday/Sunday in July) }}
'''Yasaka Shrine''' (八坂神社・八阪神社, やさかじんじゃ) refers to {{ill|Shinto shrines|ja|神社|12=draft}} named "Yasaka." It is sometimes written as {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|弥栄神社|12=draft}}, which is covered in another article.
These shrines are dedicated to {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊|12=draft}}, the deity of {{ill|Gion faith|ja|祇園信仰|12=draft}}. Before the {{ill|Shinto-Buddhism Separation Order|ja|神仏分離令|12=draft}}, Susanoo-no-Mikoto was identified with {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō|1=Gozu Tennō|12=draft}}.
Other names based on Gion faith include {{ill|Gion Shrine|ja|祇園神社|lt=Gion Shrines|12=draft}}, {{ill|Hiromine Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|広峯神社 (曖昧さ回避)|lt=Hiromine Shrines|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tennō Shrine|ja|天王神社|lt=Tennō Shrines|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tsushima Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|津島神社|lt=Tsushima Shrines|12=draft}}, {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲神社|lt=Yakumo Shrines|12=draft}}, {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|八重垣神社|lt=Yaegaki Shrines|12=draft}}, {{ill|Suga Shrine|ja|須賀神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Susanoo Shrine|ja|素盞嗚神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Susa Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|須佐神社|Susa Shrine (disambiguation)=Susa Shrine (disambiguation)|lt=Susa Shrine|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Hikawa Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|氷川神社|12=draft}}.
Notably, some exceptions include Yasaka shrines that enshrine {{ill|Yasakatome-no-Kami|ja|八坂刀売神|12=draft}}.
== Main Shrine == [[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|thumb|250px|right|Kyoto's {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|八坂神社|12=draft}}, one of the head shrines]] * '''{{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|八坂神社|12=draft}}''' ({{ill|Higashiyama Ward, Kyoto|ja|京都市東山区|12=draft}}) – Formerly {{ill|Kanjin'in Gion-sha|ja|感神院祇園社|12=draft}} under {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗|12=draft}} and {{ill|Mount Hiei|ja|比叡山|12=draft}} until the Shinto-Buddhism Separation Order. Claimed as the main shrine of Susanoo-no-Mikoto nationwide.
* ''' {{ill|Eki Shrine|ja|疫神社|12=draft}}''' – Enshrines {{ill|Somin Shōrai|ja|蘇民将来命|12=draft}}. '''Yasaka Shrine''' or '''Yasaka Jinja''' (八坂神社・八阪神社, Yasaka Jinja) refers to Shinto shrines that include "Yasaka" in their name. Some may also be written as {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|弥栄神社|12=draft}}.
These shrines are part of {{ill|Gion Faith|ja|祇園信仰|12=draft}}, venerating {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊|12=draft}} (formerly identified with {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō|1=Gozu Tennō|12=draft}} before the {{ill|Shinbutsu Bunri|ja|神仏分離|12=draft}} decree).
Other shrines based on Gion Faith include {{ill|Gion Shrine|ja|祇園神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Hiromine Shrine|ja|広峯神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tennō Shrine|ja|天王神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tsushima Shrine|ja|津島神社|12=draft}}<ref>{{ill|Tsushima Faith|ja|津島信仰|12=draft}}</ref>, {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine|ja|八重垣神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Suga Shrine|ja|須賀神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Susanoo Shrine|ja|素盞嗚神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Susa Shrine|ja|須佐神社|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Hikawa Shrine|ja|氷川神社|12=draft}}<ref>{{ill|Hikawa Faith|ja|氷川信仰|12=draft}}</ref>, among others. Their usage varies by historical period and records.
However, there are exceptions where Yasaka Shrines enshrine {{ill|Yasakatome-no-Kami|ja|八坂刀売神|12=draft}} instead.
The {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kyoto)|ja|八坂神社|12=draft}} in Higashiyama, Kyoto, claims to be the head shrine of all shrines dedicated to Susanoo-no-Mikoto. Before the Shinbutsu Bunri decree, it was known as {{ill|Kanjin-in Gion-sha|ja|感神院祇園社|12=draft}} of the {{ill|Tendai sect|ja|天台宗|12=draft}}, affiliated with {{ill|Mount Hiei|ja|比叡山|12=draft}}.
[[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kyoto)|ja|八坂神社|12=draft}} (One of the Head Shrines)]]

{{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|250px|right]] | name = Yasaka Shrine (八坂神社) | location = [[Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka]], [[Kitakyushu]], [[Kokurakita Ward]], {{ill|Jōnai|ja|城内 (北九州市)|12=draft}} | coordinates = {{Coord|33|53|07.68|N|130|52|25.39|E|region:JP-40_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Yasaka Shrine}} | Deities = {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊|12=draft}} (formerly {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō|1=Gozu Tennō|12=draft}}) | type = [[Prefectural Shrine|Ken-sha]] (as of May 15, Meiji 6) | Established = {{ill|Hosokawa Tadaoki|ja|細川忠興|12=draft}}, [[Genna (era)|Genna]] 3 (1617) | Main Hall = Nagare-zukuri | Festival = [[Kokura Gion Daiko]] (third Saturday/Sunday in July) }}
'''Yasaka Shrine''' (八坂神社・八阪神社, やさかじんじゃ) refers to {{ill|Shinto shrines|ja|神社|12=draft}} named "Yasaka." It is sometimes written as {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|弥栄神社|12=draft}}, which is covered in another article.
These shrines are dedicated to {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊|12=draft}}, the deity of {{ill|Gion faith|ja|祇園信仰|12=draft}}. Before the {{ill|Shinto-Buddhism Separation Order|ja|神仏分離令|12=draft}}, Susanoo-no-Mikoto was identified with {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō|1=Gozu Tennō|12=draft}}.
Other names based on Gion faith include {{ill|Gion Shrine|ja|祇園神社|lt=Gion Shrines|12=draft}}, {{ill|Hiromine Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|広峯神社 (曖昧さ回避)|lt=Hiromine Shrines|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tennō Shrine|ja|天王神社|lt=Tennō Shrines|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tsushima Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|津島神社|lt=Tsushima Shrines|12=draft}}, {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲神社|lt=Yakumo Shrines|12=draft}}, {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|八重垣神社|lt=Yaegaki Shrines|12=draft}}, {{ill|Suga Shrine|ja|須賀神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Susanoo Shrine|ja|素盞嗚神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Susa Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|須佐神社|Susa Shrine (disambiguation)=Susa Shrine (disambiguation)|lt=Susa Shrine|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Hikawa Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|氷川神社|12=draft}}.
Notably, some exceptions include Yasaka shrines that enshrine {{ill|Yasakatome-no-Kami|ja|八坂刀売神|12=draft}}.
== Main Shrine == [[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|thumb|250px|right|Kyoto's {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|八坂神社|12=draft}}, one of the head shrines]] * '''{{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|八坂神社|12=draft}}''' ({{ill|Higashiyama Ward, Kyoto|ja|京都市東山区|12=draft}}) – Formerly {{ill|Kanjin'in Gion-sha|ja|感神院祇園社|12=draft}} under {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗|12=draft}} and {{ill|Mount Hiei|ja|比叡山|12=draft}} until the Shinto-Buddhism Separation Order. Claimed as the main shrine of Susanoo-no-Mikoto nationwide.
* ''' {{ill|Eki Shrine|ja|疫神社|12=draft}}''' – Enshrines {{ill|Somin Shōrai|ja|蘇民将来命|12=draft}}. '''Yasaka Shrine''' or '''Yasaka Jinja''' (八坂神社・八阪神社, Yasaka Jinja) refers to Shinto shrines that include "Yasaka" in their name. Some may also be written as {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|弥栄神社|12=draft}}.
These shrines are part of {{ill|Gion Faith|ja|祇園信仰|12=draft}}, venerating {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊|12=draft}} (formerly identified with {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō|1=Gozu Tennō|12=draft}} before the {{ill|Shinbutsu Bunri|ja|神仏分離|12=draft}} decree).
Other shrines based on Gion Faith include {{ill|Gion Shrine|ja|祇園神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Hiromine Shrine|ja|広峯神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tennō Shrine|ja|天王神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tsushima Shrine|ja|津島神社|12=draft}}<ref>{{ill|Tsushima Faith|ja|津島信仰|12=draft}}</ref>, {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine|ja|八重垣神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Suga Shrine|ja|須賀神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Susanoo Shrine|ja|素盞嗚神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Susa Shrine|ja|須佐神社|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Hikawa Shrine|ja|氷川神社|12=draft}}<ref>{{ill|Hikawa Faith|ja|氷川信仰|12=draft}}</ref>, among others. Their usage varies by historical period and records.
However, there are exceptions where Yasaka Shrines enshrine {{ill|Yasakatome-no-Kami|ja|八坂刀売神|12=draft}} instead.
The {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kyoto)|ja|八坂神社|12=draft}} in Higashiyama, Kyoto, claims to be the head shrine of all shrines dedicated to Susanoo-no-Mikoto. Before the Shinbutsu Bunri decree, it was known as {{ill|Kanjin-in Gion-sha|ja|感神院祇園社|12=draft}} of the {{ill|Tendai sect|ja|天台宗|12=draft}}, affiliated with {{ill|Mount Hiei|ja|比叡山|12=draft}}.

{{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|250px|right]] | name = Yasaka Shrine (八坂神社) | location = [[Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka]], [[Kitakyushu]], [[Kokurakita Ward]], {{ill|Jōnai|ja|城内 (北九州市)|12=draft}} | coordinates = {{Coord|33|53|07.68|N|130|52|25.39|E|region:JP-40_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Yasaka Shrine}} | Deities = {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊|12=draft}} (formerly {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō|1=Gozu Tennō|12=draft}}) | type = [[Prefectural Shrine|Ken-sha]] (as of May 15, Meiji 6) | Established = {{ill|Hosokawa Tadaoki|ja|細川忠興|12=draft}}, [[Genna (era)|Genna]] 3 (1617) | Main Hall = Nagare-zukuri | Festival = [[Kokura Gion Daiko]] (third Saturday/Sunday in July) }}
'''Yasaka Shrine''' (八坂神社・八阪神社, やさかじんじゃ) refers to {{ill|Shinto shrines|ja|神社|12=draft}} named "Yasaka." It is sometimes written as {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|弥栄神社|12=draft}}, which is covered in another article.
These shrines are dedicated to {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊|12=draft}}, the deity of {{ill|Gion faith|ja|祇園信仰|12=draft}}. Before the {{ill|Shinto-Buddhism Separation Order|ja|神仏分離令|12=draft}}, Susanoo-no-Mikoto was identified with {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō|1=Gozu Tennō|12=draft}}.
Other names based on Gion faith include {{ill|Gion Shrine|ja|祇園神社|lt=Gion Shrines|12=draft}}, {{ill|Hiromine Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|広峯神社 (曖昧さ回避)|lt=Hiromine Shrines|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tennō Shrine|ja|天王神社|lt=Tennō Shrines|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tsushima Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|津島神社|lt=Tsushima Shrines|12=draft}}, {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲神社|lt=Yakumo Shrines|12=draft}}, {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|八重垣神社|lt=Yaegaki Shrines|12=draft}}, {{ill|Suga Shrine|ja|須賀神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Susanoo Shrine|ja|素盞嗚神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Susa Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|須佐神社|Susa Shrine (disambiguation)=Susa Shrine (disambiguation)|lt=Susa Shrine|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Hikawa Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|氷川神社|12=draft}}.
Notably, some exceptions include Yasaka shrines that enshrine {{ill|Yasakatome-no-Kami|ja|八坂刀売神|12=draft}}.
== Main Shrine == [[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|thumb|250px|right|Kyoto's {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|八坂神社|12=draft}}, one of the head shrines]] * '''{{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|八坂神社|12=draft}}''' ({{ill|Higashiyama Ward, Kyoto|ja|京都市東山区|12=draft}}) – Formerly {{ill|Kanjin'in Gion-sha|ja|感神院祇園社|12=draft}} under {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗|12=draft}} and {{ill|Mount Hiei|ja|比叡山|12=draft}} until the Shinto-Buddhism Separation Order. Claimed as the main shrine of Susanoo-no-Mikoto nationwide.
* ''' {{ill|Eki Shrine|ja|疫神社|12=draft}}''' – Enshrines {{ill|Somin Shōrai|ja|蘇民将来命|12=draft}}. '''Yasaka Shrine''' or '''Yasaka Jinja''' (八坂神社・八阪神社, Yasaka Jinja) refers to Shinto shrines that include "Yasaka" in their name. Some may also be written as {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|弥栄神社|12=draft}}.
These shrines are part of {{ill|Gion Faith|ja|祇園信仰|12=draft}}, venerating {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊|12=draft}} (formerly identified with {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō|1=Gozu Tennō|12=draft}} before the {{ill|Shinbutsu Bunri|ja|神仏分離|12=draft}} decree).
Other shrines based on Gion Faith include {{ill|Gion Shrine|ja|祇園神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Hiromine Shrine|ja|広峯神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tennō Shrine|ja|天王神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tsushima Shrine|ja|津島神社|12=draft}}<ref>{{ill|Tsushima Faith|ja|津島信仰|12=draft}}</ref>, {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine|ja|八重垣神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Suga Shrine|ja|須賀神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Susanoo Shrine|ja|素盞嗚神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Susa Shrine|ja|須佐神社|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Hikawa Shrine|ja|氷川神社|12=draft}}<ref>{{ill|Hikawa Faith|ja|氷川信仰|12=draft}}</ref>, among others. Their usage varies by historical period and records.
However, there are exceptions where Yasaka Shrines enshrine {{ill|Yasakatome-no-Kami|ja|八坂刀売神|12=draft}} instead.
The {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kyoto)|ja|八坂神社|12=draft}} in Higashiyama, Kyoto, claims to be the head shrine of all shrines dedicated to Susanoo-no-Mikoto. Before the Shinbutsu Bunri decree, it was known as {{ill|Kanjin-in Gion-sha|ja|感神院祇園社|12=draft}} of the {{ill|Tendai sect|ja|天台宗|12=draft}}, affiliated with {{ill|Mount Hiei|ja|比叡山|12=draft}}.
[[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kyoto)|ja|八坂神社|12=draft}} (One of the Head Shrines)]]

{{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|250px|right]] | name = Yasaka Shrine (八坂神社) | location = [[Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka]], [[Kitakyushu]], [[Kokurakita Ward]], {{ill|Jōnai|ja|城内 (北九州市)|12=draft}} | coordinates = {{Coord|33|53|07.68|N|130|52|25.39|E|region:JP-40_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Yasaka Shrine}} | Deities = {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊|12=draft}} (formerly {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō|1=Gozu Tennō|12=draft}}) | type = [[Prefectural Shrine|Ken-sha]] (as of May 15, Meiji 6) | Established = {{ill|Hosokawa Tadaoki|ja|細川忠興|12=draft}}, [[Genna (era)|Genna]] 3 (1617) | Main Hall = Nagare-zukuri | Festival = [[Kokura Gion Daiko]] (third Saturday/Sunday in July) }}
'''Yasaka Shrine''' (八坂神社・八阪神社, やさかじんじゃ) refers to {{ill|Shinto shrines|ja|神社|12=draft}} named "Yasaka." It is sometimes written as {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|弥栄神社|12=draft}}, which is covered in another article.
These shrines are dedicated to {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊|12=draft}}, the deity of {{ill|Gion faith|ja|祇園信仰|12=draft}}. Before the {{ill|Shinto-Buddhism Separation Order|ja|神仏分離令|12=draft}}, Susanoo-no-Mikoto was identified with {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō|1=Gozu Tennō|12=draft}}.
Other names based on Gion faith include {{ill|Gion Shrine|ja|祇園神社|lt=Gion Shrines|12=draft}}, {{ill|Hiromine Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|広峯神社 (曖昧さ回避)|lt=Hiromine Shrines|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tennō Shrine|ja|天王神社|lt=Tennō Shrines|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tsushima Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|津島神社|lt=Tsushima Shrines|12=draft}}, {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲神社|lt=Yakumo Shrines|12=draft}}, {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|八重垣神社|lt=Yaegaki Shrines|12=draft}}, {{ill|Suga Shrine|ja|須賀神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Susanoo Shrine|ja|素盞嗚神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Susa Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|須佐神社|Susa Shrine (disambiguation)=Susa Shrine (disambiguation)|lt=Susa Shrine|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Hikawa Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|氷川神社|12=draft}}.
Notably, some exceptions include Yasaka shrines that enshrine {{ill|Yasakatome-no-Kami|ja|八坂刀売神|12=draft}}.
== Main Shrine == [[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|thumb|250px|right|Kyoto's {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|八坂神社|12=draft}}, one of the head shrines]] * '''{{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|八坂神社|12=draft}}''' ({{ill|Higashiyama Ward, Kyoto|ja|京都市東山区|12=draft}}) – Formerly {{ill|Kanjin'in Gion-sha|ja|感神院祇園社|12=draft}} under {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗|12=draft}} and {{ill|Mount Hiei|ja|比叡山|12=draft}} until the Shinto-Buddhism Separation Order. Claimed as the main shrine of Susanoo-no-Mikoto nationwide.
* ''' {{ill|Eki Shrine|ja|疫神社|12=draft}}''' – Enshrines {{ill|Somin Shōrai|ja|蘇民将来命|12=draft}}. '''Yasaka Shrine''' or '''Yasaka Jinja''' (八坂神社・八阪神社, Yasaka Jinja) refers to Shinto shrines that include "Yasaka" in their name. Some may also be written as {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|弥栄神社|12=draft}}.
These shrines are part of {{ill|Gion Faith|ja|祇園信仰|12=draft}}, venerating {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊|12=draft}} (formerly identified with {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō|1=Gozu Tennō|12=draft}} before the {{ill|Shinbutsu Bunri|ja|神仏分離|12=draft}} decree).
Other shrines based on Gion Faith include {{ill|Gion Shrine|ja|祇園神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Hiromine Shrine|ja|広峯神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tennō Shrine|ja|天王神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tsushima Shrine|ja|津島神社|12=draft}}<ref>{{ill|Tsushima Faith|ja|津島信仰|12=draft}}</ref>, {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine|ja|八重垣神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Suga Shrine|ja|須賀神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Susanoo Shrine|ja|素盞嗚神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Susa Shrine|ja|須佐神社|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Hikawa Shrine|ja|氷川神社|12=draft}}<ref>{{ill|Hikawa Faith|ja|氷川信仰|12=draft}}</ref>, among others. Their usage varies by historical period and records.
However, there are exceptions where Yasaka Shrines enshrine {{ill|Yasakatome-no-Kami|ja|八坂刀売神|12=draft}} instead.
The {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kyoto)|ja|八坂神社|12=draft}} in Higashiyama, Kyoto, claims to be the head shrine of all shrines dedicated to Susanoo-no-Mikoto. Before the Shinbutsu Bunri decree, it was known as {{ill|Kanjin-in Gion-sha|ja|感神院祇園社|12=draft}} of the {{ill|Tendai sect|ja|天台宗|12=draft}}, affiliated with {{ill|Mount Hiei|ja|比叡山|12=draft}}.

{{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|250px|right]] | name = Yasaka Shrine (八坂神社) | location = [[Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka]], [[Kitakyushu]], [[Kokurakita Ward]], {{ill|Jōnai|ja|城内 (北九州市)|12=draft}} | coordinates = {{Coord|33|53|07.68|N|130|52|25.39|E|region:JP-40_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Yasaka Shrine}} | Deities = {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊|12=draft}} (formerly {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō|1=Gozu Tennō|12=draft}}) | type = [[Prefectural Shrine|Ken-sha]] (as of May 15, Meiji 6) | Established = {{ill|Hosokawa Tadaoki|ja|細川忠興|12=draft}}, [[Genna (era)|Genna]] 3 (1617) | Main Hall = Nagare-zukuri | Festival = [[Kokura Gion Daiko]] (third Saturday/Sunday in July) }}
'''Yasaka Shrine''' (八坂神社・八阪神社, やさかじんじゃ) refers to {{ill|Shinto shrines|ja|神社|12=draft}} named "Yasaka." It is sometimes written as {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|弥栄神社|12=draft}}, which is covered in another article.
These shrines are dedicated to {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊|12=draft}}, the deity of {{ill|Gion faith|ja|祇園信仰|12=draft}}. Before the {{ill|Shinto-Buddhism Separation Order|ja|神仏分離令|12=draft}}, Susanoo-no-Mikoto was identified with {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō|1=Gozu Tennō|12=draft}}.
Other names based on Gion faith include {{ill|Gion Shrine|ja|祇園神社|lt=Gion Shrines|12=draft}}, {{ill|Hiromine Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|広峯神社 (曖昧さ回避)|lt=Hiromine Shrines|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tennō Shrine|ja|天王神社|lt=Tennō Shrines|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tsushima Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|津島神社|lt=Tsushima Shrines|12=draft}}, {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲神社|lt=Yakumo Shrines|12=draft}}, {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|八重垣神社|lt=Yaegaki Shrines|12=draft}}, {{ill|Suga Shrine|ja|須賀神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Susanoo Shrine|ja|素盞嗚神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Susa Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|須佐神社|Susa Shrine (disambiguation)=Susa Shrine (disambiguation)|lt=Susa Shrine|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Hikawa Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|氷川神社|12=draft}}.
Notably, some exceptions include Yasaka shrines that enshrine {{ill|Yasakatome-no-Kami|ja|八坂刀売神|12=draft}}.
== Main Shrine == [[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|thumb|250px|right|Kyoto's {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|八坂神社|12=draft}}, one of the head shrines]] * '''{{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|八坂神社|12=draft}}''' ({{ill|Higashiyama Ward, Kyoto|ja|京都市東山区|12=draft}}) – Formerly {{ill|Kanjin'in Gion-sha|ja|感神院祇園社|12=draft}} under {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗|12=draft}} and {{ill|Mount Hiei|ja|比叡山|12=draft}} until the Shinto-Buddhism Separation Order. Claimed as the main shrine of Susanoo-no-Mikoto nationwide.
* ''' {{ill|Eki Shrine|ja|疫神社|12=draft}}''' – Enshrines {{ill|Somin Shōrai|ja|蘇民将来命|12=draft}}. '''Yasaka Shrine''' or '''Yasaka Jinja''' (八坂神社・八阪神社, Yasaka Jinja) refers to Shinto shrines that include "Yasaka" in their name. Some may also be written as {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|弥栄神社|12=draft}}.
These shrines are part of {{ill|Gion Faith|ja|祇園信仰|12=draft}}, venerating {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊|12=draft}} (formerly identified with {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō|1=Gozu Tennō|12=draft}} before the {{ill|Shinbutsu Bunri|ja|神仏分離|12=draft}} decree).
Other shrines based on Gion Faith include {{ill|Gion Shrine|ja|祇園神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Hiromine Shrine|ja|広峯神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tennō Shrine|ja|天王神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tsushima Shrine|ja|津島神社|12=draft}}<ref>{{ill|Tsushima Faith|ja|津島信仰|12=draft}}</ref>, {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine|ja|八重垣神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Suga Shrine|ja|須賀神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Susanoo Shrine|ja|素盞嗚神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Susa Shrine|ja|須佐神社|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Hikawa Shrine|ja|氷川神社|12=draft}}<ref>{{ill|Hikawa Faith|ja|氷川信仰|12=draft}}</ref>, among others. Their usage varies by historical period and records.
However, there are exceptions where Yasaka Shrines enshrine {{ill|Yasakatome-no-Kami|ja|八坂刀売神|12=draft}} instead.
The {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kyoto)|ja|八坂神社|12=draft}} in Higashiyama, Kyoto, claims to be the head shrine of all shrines dedicated to Susanoo-no-Mikoto. Before the Shinbutsu Bunri decree, it was known as {{ill|Kanjin-in Gion-sha|ja|感神院祇園社|12=draft}} of the {{ill|Tendai sect|ja|天台宗|12=draft}}, affiliated with {{ill|Mount Hiei|ja|比叡山|12=draft}}.

{{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|250px|right]] | name = Yasaka Shrine (八坂神社) | location = [[Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka]], [[Kitakyushu]], [[Kokurakita Ward]], {{ill|Jōnai|ja|城内 (北九州市)|12=draft}} | coordinates = {{Coord|33|53|07.68|N|130|52|25.39|E|region:JP-40_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Yasaka Shrine}} | Deities = {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊|12=draft}} (formerly {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō|1=Gozu Tennō|12=draft}}) | type = [[Prefectural Shrine|Ken-sha]] (as of May 15, Meiji 6) | Established = {{ill|Hosokawa Tadaoki|ja|細川忠興|12=draft}}, [[Genna (era)|Genna]] 3 (1617) | Main Hall = Nagare-zukuri | Festival = [[Kokura Gion Daiko]] (third Saturday/Sunday in July) }}
'''Yasaka Shrine''' (八坂神社・八阪神社, やさかじんじゃ) refers to {{ill|Shinto shrines|ja|神社|12=draft}} named "Yasaka." It is sometimes written as {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|弥栄神社|12=draft}}, which is covered in another article.
These shrines are dedicated to {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊|12=draft}}, the deity of {{ill|Gion faith|ja|祇園信仰|12=draft}}. Before the {{ill|Shinto-Buddhism Separation Order|ja|神仏分離令|12=draft}}, Susanoo-no-Mikoto was identified with {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō|1=Gozu Tennō|12=draft}}.
Other names based on Gion faith include {{ill|Gion Shrine|ja|祇園神社|lt=Gion Shrines|12=draft}}, {{ill|Hiromine Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|広峯神社 (曖昧さ回避)|lt=Hiromine Shrines|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tennō Shrine|ja|天王神社|lt=Tennō Shrines|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tsushima Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|津島神社|lt=Tsushima Shrines|12=draft}}, {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲神社|lt=Yakumo Shrines|12=draft}}, {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|八重垣神社|lt=Yaegaki Shrines|12=draft}}, {{ill|Suga Shrine|ja|須賀神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Susanoo Shrine|ja|素盞嗚神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Susa Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|須佐神社|Susa Shrine (disambiguation)=Susa Shrine (disambiguation)|lt=Susa Shrine|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Hikawa Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|氷川神社|12=draft}}.
Notably, some exceptions include Yasaka shrines that enshrine {{ill|Yasakatome-no-Kami|ja|八坂刀売神|12=draft}}.
== Main Shrine == [[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|thumb|250px|right|Kyoto's {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|八坂神社|12=draft}}, one of the head shrines]] * '''{{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|八坂神社|12=draft}}''' ({{ill|Higashiyama Ward, Kyoto|ja|京都市東山区|12=draft}}) – Formerly {{ill|Kanjin'in Gion-sha|ja|感神院祇園社|12=draft}} under {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗|12=draft}} and {{ill|Mount Hiei|ja|比叡山|12=draft}} until the Shinto-Buddhism Separation Order. Claimed as the main shrine of Susanoo-no-Mikoto nationwide.
* ''' {{ill|Eki Shrine|ja|疫神社|12=draft}}''' – Enshrines {{ill|Somin Shōrai|ja|蘇民将来命|12=draft}}. '''Yasaka Shrine''' or '''Yasaka Jinja''' (八坂神社・八阪神社, Yasaka Jinja) refers to Shinto shrines that include "Yasaka" in their name. Some may also be written as {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|弥栄神社|12=draft}}.
These shrines are part of {{ill|Gion Faith|ja|祇園信仰|12=draft}}, venerating {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊|12=draft}} (formerly identified with {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō|1=Gozu Tennō|12=draft}} before the {{ill|Shinbutsu Bunri|ja|神仏分離|12=draft}} decree).
Other shrines based on Gion Faith include {{ill|Gion Shrine|ja|祇園神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Hiromine Shrine|ja|広峯神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tennō Shrine|ja|天王神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tsushima Shrine|ja|津島神社|12=draft}}<ref>{{ill|Tsushima Faith|ja|津島信仰|12=draft}}</ref>, {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine|ja|八重垣神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Suga Shrine|ja|須賀神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Susanoo Shrine|ja|素盞嗚神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Susa Shrine|ja|須佐神社|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Hikawa Shrine|ja|氷川神社|12=draft}}<ref>{{ill|Hikawa Faith|ja|氷川信仰|12=draft}}</ref>, among others. Their usage varies by historical period and records.
However, there are exceptions where Yasaka Shrines enshrine {{ill|Yasakatome-no-Kami|ja|八坂刀売神|12=draft}} instead.
The {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kyoto)|ja|八坂神社|12=draft}} in Higashiyama, Kyoto, claims to be the head shrine of all shrines dedicated to Susanoo-no-Mikoto. Before the Shinbutsu Bunri decree, it was known as {{ill|Kanjin-in Gion-sha|ja|感神院祇園社|12=draft}} of the {{ill|Tendai sect|ja|天台宗|12=draft}}, affiliated with {{ill|Mount Hiei|ja|比叡山|12=draft}}.
[[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kyoto)|ja|八坂神社|12=draft}} (One of the Head Shrines)]]

'''Yasaka Shrine''' (八坂神社・八阪神社, やさかじんじゃ) refers to {{ill|Shinto shrines|ja|神社|12=draft|12=draft}} named "Yasaka." It is sometimes written as {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|弥栄神社|12=draft|12=draft}}, which is covered in another article.
These shrines are dedicated to {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊|12=draft|12=draft}}, the deity of {{ill|Gion faith|ja|祇園信仰|12=draft|12=draft}}. Before the {{ill|Shinto-Buddhism Separation Order|ja|神仏分離令|12=draft|12=draft}}, Susanoo-no-Mikoto was identified with {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō|1=Gozu Tennō|12=draft|12=draft}}.
Other names based on Gion faith include {{ill|Gion Shrine|ja|祇園神社|lt=Gion Shrines|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Hiromine Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|広峯神社 (曖昧さ回避)|lt=Hiromine Shrines|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tennō Shrine|ja|天王神社|lt=Tennō Shrines|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tsushima Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|津島神社|lt=Tsushima Shrines|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲神社|lt=Yakumo Shrines|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|八重垣神社|lt=Yaegaki Shrines|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Suga Shrine|ja|須賀神社|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Susanoo Shrine|ja|素盞嗚神社|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Susa Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|須佐神社|Susa Shrine (disambiguation)=Susa Shrine (disambiguation)|lt=Susa Shrine|12=draft|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Hikawa Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|氷川神社|12=draft|12=draft}}.
Notably, some exceptions include Yasaka shrines that enshrine {{ill|Yasakatome-no-Kami|ja|八坂刀売神|12=draft|12=draft}}.
== Main Shrine == [[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|thumb|250px|right|Kyoto's {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|八坂神社|12=draft|12=draft}}, one of the head shrines]] * '''{{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|八坂神社|12=draft|12=draft}}''' ({{ill|Higashiyama Ward, Kyoto|ja|京都市東山区|12=draft|12=draft}}) – Formerly {{ill|Kanjin'in Gion-sha|ja|感神院祇園社|12=draft|12=draft}} under {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Mount Hiei|ja|比叡山|12=draft|12=draft}} until the Shinto-Buddhism Separation Order. Claimed as the main shrine of Susanoo-no-Mikoto nationwide.
* ''' {{ill|Eki Shrine|ja|疫神社|12=draft|12=draft}}''' – Enshrines {{ill|Somin Shōrai|ja|蘇民将来命|12=draft|12=draft}}. '''Yasaka Shrine''' or '''Yasaka Jinja''' (八坂神社・八阪神社, Yasaka Jinja) refers to Shinto shrines that include "Yasaka" in their name. Some may also be written as {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|弥栄神社|12=draft|12=draft}}.
These shrines are part of {{ill|Gion Faith|ja|祇園信仰|12=draft|12=draft}}, venerating {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊|12=draft|12=draft}} (formerly identified with {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō|1=Gozu Tennō|12=draft|12=draft}} before the {{ill|Shinbutsu Bunri|ja|神仏分離|12=draft|12=draft}} decree).
Other shrines based on Gion Faith include {{ill|Gion Shrine|ja|祇園神社|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Hiromine Shrine|ja|広峯神社|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tennō Shrine|ja|天王神社|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tsushima Shrine|ja|津島神社|12=draft|12=draft}}<ref>{{ill|Tsushima Faith|ja|津島信仰|12=draft|12=draft}}</ref>, {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲神社|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine|ja|八重垣神社|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Suga Shrine|ja|須賀神社|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Susanoo Shrine|ja|素盞嗚神社|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Susa Shrine|ja|須佐神社|12=draft|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Hikawa Shrine|ja|氷川神社|12=draft|12=draft}}<ref>{{ill|Hikawa Faith|ja|氷川信仰|12=draft|12=draft}}</ref>, among others. Their usage varies by historical period and records.
However, there are exceptions where Yasaka Shrines enshrine {{ill|Yasakatome-no-Kami|ja|八坂刀売神|12=draft|12=draft}} instead.
The {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kyoto)|ja|八坂神社|12=draft|12=draft}} in Higashiyama, Kyoto, claims to be the head shrine of all shrines dedicated to Susanoo-no-Mikoto. Before the Shinbutsu Bunri decree, it was known as {{ill|Kanjin-in Gion-sha|ja|感神院祇園社|12=draft|12=draft}} of the {{ill|Tendai sect|ja|天台宗|12=draft|12=draft}}, affiliated with {{ill|Mount Hiei|ja|比叡山|12=draft|12=draft}}.
[[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kyoto)|ja|八坂神社|12=draft|12=draft}} (One of the Head Shrines)]]

These shrines are dedicated to {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊|12=draft|12=draft}}, the deity of {{ill|Gion faith|ja|祇園信仰|12=draft|12=draft}}. Before the {{ill|Shinto-Buddhism Separation Order|ja|神仏分離令|12=draft|12=draft}}, Susanoo-no-Mikoto was identified with {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō|1=Gozu Tennō|12=draft|12=draft}}.
Other names based on Gion faith include {{ill|Gion Shrine|ja|祇園神社|lt=Gion Shrines|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Hiromine Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|広峯神社 (曖昧さ回避)|lt=Hiromine Shrines|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tennō Shrine|ja|天王神社|lt=Tennō Shrines|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tsushima Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|津島神社|lt=Tsushima Shrines|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲神社|lt=Yakumo Shrines|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|八重垣神社|lt=Yaegaki Shrines|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Suga Shrine|ja|須賀神社|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Susanoo Shrine|ja|素盞嗚神社|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Susa Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|須佐神社|Susa Shrine (disambiguation)=Susa Shrine (disambiguation)|lt=Susa Shrine|12=draft|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Hikawa Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|氷川神社|12=draft|12=draft}}.
Notably, some exceptions include Yasaka shrines that enshrine {{ill|Yasakatome-no-Kami|ja|八坂刀売神|12=draft|12=draft}}.
== Main Shrine == [[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|thumb|250px|right|Kyoto's {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|八坂神社|12=draft|12=draft}}, one of the head shrines]] * '''{{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|八坂神社|12=draft|12=draft}}''' ({{ill|Higashiyama Ward, Kyoto|ja|京都市東山区|12=draft|12=draft}}) – Formerly {{ill|Kanjin'in Gion-sha|ja|感神院祇園社|12=draft|12=draft}} under {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Mount Hiei|ja|比叡山|12=draft|12=draft}} until the Shinto-Buddhism Separation Order. Claimed as the main shrine of Susanoo-no-Mikoto nationwide.
* ''' {{ill|Eki Shrine|ja|疫神社|12=draft|12=draft}}''' – Enshrines {{ill|Somin Shōrai|ja|蘇民将来命|12=draft|12=draft}}. '''Yasaka Shrine''' or '''Yasaka Jinja''' (八坂神社・八阪神社, Yasaka Jinja) refers to Shinto shrines that include "Yasaka" in their name. Some may also be written as {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|弥栄神社|12=draft|12=draft}}.
These shrines are part of {{ill|Gion Faith|ja|祇園信仰|12=draft|12=draft}}, venerating {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊|12=draft|12=draft}} (formerly identified with {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō|1=Gozu Tennō|12=draft|12=draft}} before the {{ill|Shinbutsu Bunri|ja|神仏分離|12=draft|12=draft}} decree).
Other shrines based on Gion Faith include {{ill|Gion Shrine|ja|祇園神社|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Hiromine Shrine|ja|広峯神社|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tennō Shrine|ja|天王神社|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tsushima Shrine|ja|津島神社|12=draft|12=draft}}<ref>{{ill|Tsushima Faith|ja|津島信仰|12=draft|12=draft}}</ref>, {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲神社|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine|ja|八重垣神社|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Suga Shrine|ja|須賀神社|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Susanoo Shrine|ja|素盞嗚神社|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Susa Shrine|ja|須佐神社|12=draft|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Hikawa Shrine|ja|氷川神社|12=draft|12=draft}}<ref>{{ill|Hikawa Faith|ja|氷川信仰|12=draft|12=draft}}</ref>, among others. Their usage varies by historical period and records.
However, there are exceptions where Yasaka Shrines enshrine {{ill|Yasakatome-no-Kami|ja|八坂刀売神|12=draft|12=draft}} instead.
The {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kyoto)|ja|八坂神社|12=draft|12=draft}} in Higashiyama, Kyoto, claims to be the head shrine of all shrines dedicated to Susanoo-no-Mikoto. Before the Shinbutsu Bunri decree, it was known as {{ill|Kanjin-in Gion-sha|ja|感神院祇園社|12=draft|12=draft}} of the {{ill|Tendai sect|ja|天台宗|12=draft|12=draft}}, affiliated with {{ill|Mount Hiei|ja|比叡山|12=draft|12=draft}}.

Other names based on Gion faith include {{ill|Gion Shrine|ja|祇園神社|lt=Gion Shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Hiromine Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|広峯神社 (曖昧さ回避)|lt=Hiromine Shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Tennō Shrine|ja|天王神社|lt=Tennō Shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Tsushima Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|津島神社|lt=Tsushima Shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲神社|lt=Yakumo Shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|八重垣神社|lt=Yaegaki Shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Suga Shrine|ja|須賀神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Susanoo Shrine|ja|素盞嗚神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Susa Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|須佐神社|Susa Shrine (disambiguation)=Susa Shrine (disambiguation)|lt=Susa Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and {{ill|Hikawa Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|氷川神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.
Notably, some exceptions include Yasaka shrines that enshrine {{ill|Yasakatome-no-Kami|ja|八坂刀売神|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.
== Main Shrine == [[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|thumb|250px|right|Kyoto's {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|八坂神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, one of the head shrines]] * '''{{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|八坂神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''' ({{ill|Higashiyama Ward, Kyoto|ja|京都市東山区|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) – Formerly {{ill|Kanjin'in Gion-sha|ja|感神院祇園社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} under {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Mount Hiei|ja|比叡山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} until the Shinto-Buddhism Separation Order. Claimed as the main shrine of Susanoo-no-Mikoto nationwide.
* ''' {{ill|Eki Shrine|ja|疫神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''' – Enshrines {{ill|Somin Shōrai|ja|蘇民将来命|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. '''Yasaka Shrine''' or '''Yasaka Jinja''' (八坂神社・八阪神社, Yasaka Jinja) refers to Shinto shrines that include "Yasaka" in their name. Some may also be written as {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|弥栄神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.
These shrines are part of {{ill|Gion Faith|ja|祇園信仰|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, venerating {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (formerly identified with {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō|1=Gozu Tennō|qq=draft|qq=draft}} before the {{ill|Shinbutsu Bunri|ja|神仏分離|qq=draft|qq=draft}} decree).
Other shrines based on Gion Faith include {{ill|Gion Shrine|ja|祇園神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Hiromine Shrine|ja|広峯神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Tennō Shrine|ja|天王神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Tsushima Shrine|ja|津島神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}<ref>{{ill|Tsushima Faith|ja|津島信仰|qq=draft|qq=draft}}</ref>, {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine|ja|八重垣神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Suga Shrine|ja|須賀神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Susanoo Shrine|ja|素盞嗚神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Susa Shrine|ja|須佐神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and {{ill|Hikawa Shrine|ja|氷川神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}<ref>{{ill|Hikawa Faith|ja|氷川信仰|qq=draft|qq=draft}}</ref>, among others. Their usage varies by historical period and records.
However, there are exceptions where Yasaka Shrines enshrine {{ill|Yasakatome-no-Kami|ja|八坂刀売神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} instead.
The {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kyoto)|ja|八坂神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Higashiyama, Kyoto, claims to be the head shrine of all shrines dedicated to Susanoo-no-Mikoto. Before the Shinbutsu Bunri decree, it was known as {{ill|Kanjin-in Gion-sha|ja|感神院祇園社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} of the {{ill|Tendai sect|ja|天台宗|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, affiliated with {{ill|Mount Hiei|ja|比叡山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.
[[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kyoto)|ja|八坂神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (One of the Head Shrines)]]

revision.text:
'''八坂神社'''・'''八阪神社'''（やさかじんじゃ）は、｢八坂」を社名に持つ[[神社]]。[[弥栄神社]]と表記する場合もある。素戔嗚尊（[[スサノオ]]）を祭神（[[神仏分離]]令までは[[牛頭天王]]）とする[[祇園信仰]]の神社である。
他に祇園信仰に基づく神社名称としては、[[祇園神社]]（祇園社）、[[広峯神社 (曖昧さ回避)|広峯神社]]、[[天王神社]]（天王社）、[[津島神社 (曖昧さ回避)|津島神社]]<ref>[[津島信仰]]</ref>、[[八雲神社]]、[[八重垣神社 (曖昧さ回避)|八重垣神社]]、[[須賀神社]]、[[素盞嗚神社]]、[[須佐神社]]、[[氷川神社 (曖昧さ回避)|氷川神社]]<ref>[[氷川信仰]]</ref>などがあり、時代や資料によって用いられる。ただし例外として[[八坂刀売神]]を祀る八坂神社も存在する。
京都市東山区の[[八坂神社]]は、全国の素戔嗚尊を祭神とする神社の総本社と主張している。神仏分離令までは[[天台宗]][[比叡山]]感神院祇園社。
[[ファイル:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|thumb|250px|right|京都の[[八坂神社]]（総本社の一つ）]]

revision.text:
'''八坂神社'''・'''八阪神社'''（やさかじんじゃ）は、｢八坂」を社名に持つ[[神社]]。[[弥栄神社]]と表記する場合もある。素戔嗚尊（[[スサノオ]]）を祭神（[[神仏分離]]令までは[[牛頭天王]]）とする[[祇園信仰]]の神社である。
他に祇園信仰に基づく神社名称としては、[[祇園神社]]（祇園社）、[[広峯神社 (曖昧さ回避)|広峯神社]]、[[天王神社]]（天王社）、[[津島神社 (曖昧さ回避)|津島神社]]<ref>[[津島信仰]]</ref>、[[八雲神社]]、[[八重垣神社 (曖昧さ回避)|八重垣神社]]、[[須賀神社]]、[[素盞嗚神社]]、[[須佐神社]]、[[氷川神社 (曖昧さ回避)|氷川神社]]<ref>[[氷川信仰]]</ref>などがあり、時代や資料によって用いられる。ただし例外として[[八坂刀売神]]を祀る八坂神社も存在する。
京都市東山区の[[八坂神社]]は、全国の素戔嗚尊を祭神とする神社の総本社と主張している。神仏分離令までは[[天台宗]][[比叡山]]感神院祇園社。
[[ファイル:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|thumb|250px|right|京都の[[八坂神社]]（総本社の一つ）]]

{{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|250px|right]] | name = Yasaka Shrine (八坂神社) | location = [[Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka]], [[Kitakyushu]], [[Kokurakita Ward]], {{ill|Jōnai|ja|城内 (北九州市)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} | coordinates = {{Coord|33|53|07.68|N|130|52|25.39|E|region:JP-40_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Yasaka Shrine}} | Deities = {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (formerly {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō|1=Gozu Tennō|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) | type = [[Prefectural Shrine|Ken-sha]] (as of May 15, Meiji 6) | Established = {{ill|Hosokawa Tadaoki|ja|細川忠興|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, [[Genna (era)|Genna]] 3 (1617) | Main Hall = Nagare-zukuri | Festival = [[Kokura Gion Daiko]] (third Saturday/Sunday in July) }}
'''Yasaka Shrine''' (八坂神社・八阪神社, やさかじんじゃ) refers to {{ill|Shinto shrines|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} named "Yasaka." It is sometimes written as {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|弥栄神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, which is covered in another article.
These shrines are dedicated to {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the deity of {{ill|Gion faith|ja|祇園信仰|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Before the {{ill|Shinto-Buddhism Separation Order|ja|神仏分離令|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Susanoo-no-Mikoto was identified with {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō|1=Gozu Tennō|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.
Other names based on Gion faith include {{ill|Gion Shrine|ja|祇園神社|lt=Gion Shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Hiromine Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|広峯神社 (曖昧さ回避)|lt=Hiromine Shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Tennō Shrine|ja|天王神社|lt=Tennō Shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Tsushima Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|津島神社|lt=Tsushima Shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲神社|lt=Yakumo Shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|八重垣神社|lt=Yaegaki Shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Suga Shrine|ja|須賀神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Susanoo Shrine|ja|素盞嗚神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Susa Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|須佐神社|Susa Shrine (disambiguation)=Susa Shrine (disambiguation)|lt=Susa Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and {{ill|Hikawa Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|氷川神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.
Notably, some exceptions include Yasaka shrines that enshrine {{ill|Yasakatome-no-Kami|ja|八坂刀売神|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.
== Main Shrine == [[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|thumb|250px|right|Kyoto's {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|八坂神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, one of the head shrines]] * '''{{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|八坂神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''' ({{ill|Higashiyama Ward, Kyoto|ja|京都市東山区|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) – Formerly {{ill|Kanjin'in Gion-sha|ja|感神院祇園社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} under {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Mount Hiei|ja|比叡山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} until the Shinto-Buddhism Separation Order. Claimed as the main shrine of Susanoo-no-Mikoto nationwide.
* ''' {{ill|Eki Shrine|ja|疫神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''' – Enshrines {{ill|Somin Shōrai|ja|蘇民将来命|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. '''Yasaka Shrine''' or '''Yasaka Jinja''' (八坂神社・八阪神社, Yasaka Jinja) refers to Shinto shrines that include "Yasaka" in their name. Some may also be written as {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|弥栄神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.
These shrines are part of {{ill|Gion Faith|ja|祇園信仰|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, venerating {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (formerly identified with {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō|1=Gozu Tennō|qq=draft|qq=draft}} before the {{ill|Shinbutsu Bunri|ja|神仏分離|qq=draft|qq=draft}} decree).
Other shrines based on Gion Faith include {{ill|Gion Shrine|ja|祇園神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Hiromine Shrine|ja|広峯神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Tennō Shrine|ja|天王神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Tsushima Shrine|ja|津島神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}<ref>{{ill|Tsushima Faith|ja|津島信仰|qq=draft|qq=draft}}</ref>, {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine|ja|八重垣神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Suga Shrine|ja|須賀神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Susanoo Shrine|ja|素盞嗚神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Susa Shrine|ja|須佐神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and {{ill|Hikawa Shrine|ja|氷川神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}<ref>{{ill|Hikawa Faith|ja|氷川信仰|qq=draft|qq=draft}}</ref>, among others. Their usage varies by historical period and records.
However, there are exceptions where Yasaka Shrines enshrine {{ill|Yasakatome-no-Kami|ja|八坂刀売神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} instead.
The {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kyoto)|ja|八坂神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Higashiyama, Kyoto, claims to be the head shrine of all shrines dedicated to Susanoo-no-Mikoto. Before the Shinbutsu Bunri decree, it was known as {{ill|Kanjin-in Gion-sha|ja|感神院祇園社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} of the {{ill|Tendai sect|ja|天台宗|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, affiliated with {{ill|Mount Hiei|ja|比叡山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.

{{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|250px|right]] | name = Yasaka Shrine (八坂神社) | location = [[Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka]], [[Kitakyushu]], [[Kokurakita Ward]], {{ill|Jōnai|ja|城内 (北九州市)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} | coordinates = {{Coord|33|53|07.68|N|130|52|25.39|E|region:JP-40_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Yasaka Shrine}} | Deities = {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (formerly {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō|1=Gozu Tennō|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) | type = [[Prefectural Shrine|Ken-sha]] (as of May 15, Meiji 6) | Established = {{ill|Hosokawa Tadaoki|ja|細川忠興|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, [[Genna (era)|Genna]] 3 (1617) | Main Hall = Nagare-zukuri | Festival = [[Kokura Gion Daiko]] (third Saturday/Sunday in July) }}
'''Yasaka Shrine''' (八坂神社・八阪神社, やさかじんじゃ) refers to {{ill|Shinto shrines|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} named "Yasaka." It is sometimes written as {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|弥栄神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, which is covered in another article.
These shrines are dedicated to {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the deity of {{ill|Gion faith|ja|祇園信仰|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Before the {{ill|Shinto-Buddhism Separation Order|ja|神仏分離令|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Susanoo-no-Mikoto was identified with {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō|1=Gozu Tennō|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.
Other names based on Gion faith include {{ill|Gion Shrine|ja|祇園神社|lt=Gion Shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Hiromine Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|広峯神社 (曖昧さ回避)|lt=Hiromine Shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Tennō Shrine|ja|天王神社|lt=Tennō Shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Tsushima Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|津島神社|lt=Tsushima Shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲神社|lt=Yakumo Shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|八重垣神社|lt=Yaegaki Shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Suga Shrine|ja|須賀神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Susanoo Shrine|ja|素盞嗚神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Susa Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|須佐神社|Susa Shrine (disambiguation)=Susa Shrine (disambiguation)|lt=Susa Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and {{ill|Hikawa Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|氷川神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.
Notably, some exceptions include Yasaka shrines that enshrine {{ill|Yasakatome-no-Kami|ja|八坂刀売神|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.
== Main Shrine == [[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|thumb|250px|right|Kyoto's {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|八坂神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, one of the head shrines]] * '''{{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|八坂神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''' ({{ill|Higashiyama Ward, Kyoto|ja|京都市東山区|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) – Formerly {{ill|Kanjin'in Gion-sha|ja|感神院祇園社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} under {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Mount Hiei|ja|比叡山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} until the Shinto-Buddhism Separation Order. Claimed as the main shrine of Susanoo-no-Mikoto nationwide.
* ''' {{ill|Eki Shrine|ja|疫神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''' – Enshrines {{ill|Somin Shōrai|ja|蘇民将来命|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. '''Yasaka Shrine''' or '''Yasaka Jinja''' (八坂神社・八阪神社, Yasaka Jinja) refers to Shinto shrines that include "Yasaka" in their name. Some may also be written as {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|弥栄神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.
These shrines are part of {{ill|Gion Faith|ja|祇園信仰|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, venerating {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (formerly identified with {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō|1=Gozu Tennō|qq=draft|qq=draft}} before the {{ill|Shinbutsu Bunri|ja|神仏分離|qq=draft|qq=draft}} decree).
Other shrines based on Gion Faith include {{ill|Gion Shrine|ja|祇園神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Hiromine Shrine|ja|広峯神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Tennō Shrine|ja|天王神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Tsushima Shrine|ja|津島神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}<ref>{{ill|Tsushima Faith|ja|津島信仰|qq=draft|qq=draft}}</ref>, {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine|ja|八重垣神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Suga Shrine|ja|須賀神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Susanoo Shrine|ja|素盞嗚神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Susa Shrine|ja|須佐神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and {{ill|Hikawa Shrine|ja|氷川神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}<ref>{{ill|Hikawa Faith|ja|氷川信仰|qq=draft|qq=draft}}</ref>, among others. Their usage varies by historical period and records.
However, there are exceptions where Yasaka Shrines enshrine {{ill|Yasakatome-no-Kami|ja|八坂刀売神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} instead.
The {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kyoto)|ja|八坂神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Higashiyama, Kyoto, claims to be the head shrine of all shrines dedicated to Susanoo-no-Mikoto. Before the Shinbutsu Bunri decree, it was known as {{ill|Kanjin-in Gion-sha|ja|感神院祇園社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} of the {{ill|Tendai sect|ja|天台宗|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, affiliated with {{ill|Mount Hiei|ja|比叡山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.

{{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|250px|right]] | name = Yasaka Shrine (八坂神社) | location = [[Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka]], [[Kitakyushu]], [[Kokurakita Ward]], {{ill|Jōnai|ja|城内 (北九州市)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} | coordinates = {{Coord|33|53|07.68|N|130|52|25.39|E|region:JP-40_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Yasaka Shrine}} | Deities = {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (formerly {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō|1=Gozu Tennō|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) | type = [[Prefectural Shrine|Ken-sha]] (as of May 15, Meiji 6) | Established = {{ill|Hosokawa Tadaoki|ja|細川忠興|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, [[Genna (era)|Genna]] 3 (1617) | Main Hall = Nagare-zukuri | Festival = [[Kokura Gion Daiko]] (third Saturday/Sunday in July) }}
'''Yasaka Shrine''' (八坂神社・八阪神社, やさかじんじゃ) refers to {{ill|Shinto shrines|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} named "Yasaka." It is sometimes written as {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|弥栄神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, which is covered in another article.
These shrines are dedicated to {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the deity of {{ill|Gion faith|ja|祇園信仰|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Before the {{ill|Shinto-Buddhism Separation Order|ja|神仏分離令|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Susanoo-no-Mikoto was identified with {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō|1=Gozu Tennō|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.
Other names based on Gion faith include {{ill|Gion Shrine|ja|祇園神社|lt=Gion Shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Hiromine Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|広峯神社 (曖昧さ回避)|lt=Hiromine Shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Tennō Shrine|ja|天王神社|lt=Tennō Shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Tsushima Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|津島神社|lt=Tsushima Shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲神社|lt=Yakumo Shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|八重垣神社|lt=Yaegaki Shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Suga Shrine|ja|須賀神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Susanoo Shrine|ja|素盞嗚神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Susa Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|須佐神社|Susa Shrine (disambiguation)=Susa Shrine (disambiguation)|lt=Susa Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and {{ill|Hikawa Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|氷川神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.
Notably, some exceptions include Yasaka shrines that enshrine {{ill|Yasakatome-no-Kami|ja|八坂刀売神|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.
== Main Shrine == [[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|thumb|250px|right|Kyoto's {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|八坂神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, one of the head shrines]] * '''{{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|八坂神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''' ({{ill|Higashiyama Ward, Kyoto|ja|京都市東山区|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) – Formerly {{ill|Kanjin'in Gion-sha|ja|感神院祇園社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} under {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Mount Hiei|ja|比叡山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} until the Shinto-Buddhism Separation Order. Claimed as the main shrine of Susanoo-no-Mikoto nationwide.
* ''' {{ill|Eki Shrine|ja|疫神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''' – Enshrines {{ill|Somin Shōrai|ja|蘇民将来命|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. '''Yasaka Shrine''' or '''Yasaka Jinja''' (八坂神社・八阪神社, Yasaka Jinja) refers to Shinto shrines that include "Yasaka" in their name. Some may also be written as {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|弥栄神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.
These shrines are part of {{ill|Gion Faith|ja|祇園信仰|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, venerating {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (formerly identified with {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō|1=Gozu Tennō|qq=draft|qq=draft}} before the {{ill|Shinbutsu Bunri|ja|神仏分離|qq=draft|qq=draft}} decree).
Other shrines based on Gion Faith include {{ill|Gion Shrine|ja|祇園神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Hiromine Shrine|ja|広峯神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Tennō Shrine|ja|天王神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Tsushima Shrine|ja|津島神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}<ref>{{ill|Tsushima Faith|ja|津島信仰|qq=draft|qq=draft}}</ref>, {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine|ja|八重垣神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Suga Shrine|ja|須賀神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Susanoo Shrine|ja|素盞嗚神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Susa Shrine|ja|須佐神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and {{ill|Hikawa Shrine|ja|氷川神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}<ref>{{ill|Hikawa Faith|ja|氷川信仰|qq=draft|qq=draft}}</ref>, among others. Their usage varies by historical period and records.
However, there are exceptions where Yasaka Shrines enshrine {{ill|Yasakatome-no-Kami|ja|八坂刀売神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} instead.
The {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kyoto)|ja|八坂神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Higashiyama, Kyoto, claims to be the head shrine of all shrines dedicated to Susanoo-no-Mikoto. Before the Shinbutsu Bunri decree, it was known as {{ill|Kanjin-in Gion-sha|ja|感神院祇園社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} of the {{ill|Tendai sect|ja|天台宗|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, affiliated with {{ill|Mount Hiei|ja|比叡山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.

{{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|250px|right]] | name = Yasaka Shrine (八坂神社) | location = [[Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka]], [[Kitakyushu]], [[Kokurakita Ward]], {{ill|Jōnai|ja|城内 (北九州市)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} | coordinates = {{Coord|33|53|07.68|N|130|52|25.39|E|region:JP-40_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Yasaka Shrine}} | Deities = {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (formerly {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō|1=Gozu Tennō|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) | type = [[Prefectural Shrine|Ken-sha]] (as of May 15, Meiji 6) | Established = {{ill|Hosokawa Tadaoki|ja|細川忠興|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, [[Genna (era)|Genna]] 3 (1617) | Main Hall = Nagare-zukuri | Festival = [[Kokura Gion Daiko]] (third Saturday/Sunday in July) }}
'''Yasaka Shrine''' (八坂神社・八阪神社, やさかじんじゃ) refers to {{ill|Shinto shrines|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} named "Yasaka." It is sometimes written as {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|弥栄神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, which is covered in another article.
These shrines are dedicated to {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the deity of {{ill|Gion faith|ja|祇園信仰|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Before the {{ill|Shinto-Buddhism Separation Order|ja|神仏分離令|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Susanoo-no-Mikoto was identified with {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō|1=Gozu Tennō|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.
Other names based on Gion faith include {{ill|Gion Shrine|ja|祇園神社|lt=Gion Shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Hiromine Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|広峯神社 (曖昧さ回避)|lt=Hiromine Shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Tennō Shrine|ja|天王神社|lt=Tennō Shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Tsushima Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|津島神社|lt=Tsushima Shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲神社|lt=Yakumo Shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|八重垣神社|lt=Yaegaki Shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Suga Shrine|ja|須賀神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Susanoo Shrine|ja|素盞嗚神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Susa Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|須佐神社|Susa Shrine (disambiguation)=Susa Shrine (disambiguation)|lt=Susa Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and {{ill|Hikawa Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|氷川神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.
Notably, some exceptions include Yasaka shrines that enshrine {{ill|Yasakatome-no-Kami|ja|八坂刀売神|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.
== Main Shrine == [[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|thumb|250px|right|Kyoto's {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|八坂神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, one of the head shrines]] * '''{{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|八坂神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''' ({{ill|Higashiyama Ward, Kyoto|ja|京都市東山区|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) – Formerly {{ill|Kanjin'in Gion-sha|ja|感神院祇園社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} under {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Mount Hiei|ja|比叡山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} until the Shinto-Buddhism Separation Order. Claimed as the main shrine of Susanoo-no-Mikoto nationwide.
* ''' {{ill|Eki Shrine|ja|疫神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''' – Enshrines {{ill|Somin Shōrai|ja|蘇民将来命|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. '''Yasaka Shrine''' or '''Yasaka Jinja''' (八坂神社・八阪神社, Yasaka Jinja) refers to Shinto shrines that include "Yasaka" in their name. Some may also be written as {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|弥栄神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.
These shrines are part of {{ill|Gion Faith|ja|祇園信仰|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, venerating {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (formerly identified with {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō|1=Gozu Tennō|qq=draft|qq=draft}} before the {{ill|Shinbutsu Bunri|ja|神仏分離|qq=draft|qq=draft}} decree).
Other shrines based on Gion Faith include {{ill|Gion Shrine|ja|祇園神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Hiromine Shrine|ja|広峯神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Tennō Shrine|ja|天王神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Tsushima Shrine|ja|津島神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}<ref>{{ill|Tsushima Faith|ja|津島信仰|qq=draft|qq=draft}}</ref>, {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine|ja|八重垣神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Suga Shrine|ja|須賀神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Susanoo Shrine|ja|素盞嗚神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Susa Shrine|ja|須佐神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and {{ill|Hikawa Shrine|ja|氷川神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}<ref>{{ill|Hikawa Faith|ja|氷川信仰|qq=draft|qq=draft}}</ref>, among others. Their usage varies by historical period and records.
However, there are exceptions where Yasaka Shrines enshrine {{ill|Yasakatome-no-Kami|ja|八坂刀売神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} instead.
The {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kyoto)|ja|八坂神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Higashiyama, Kyoto, claims to be the head shrine of all shrines dedicated to Susanoo-no-Mikoto. Before the Shinbutsu Bunri decree, it was known as {{ill|Kanjin-in Gion-sha|ja|感神院祇園社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} of the {{ill|Tendai sect|ja|天台宗|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, affiliated with {{ill|Mount Hiei|ja|比叡山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.

{{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|250px|right]] | name = Yasaka Shrine (八坂神社) | location = [[Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka]], [[Kitakyushu]], [[Kokurakita Ward]], {{ill|Jōnai|ja|城内 (北九州市)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} | coordinates = {{Coord|33|53|07.68|N|130|52|25.39|E|region:JP-40_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Yasaka Shrine}} | Deities = {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (formerly {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō|1=Gozu Tennō|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) | type = [[Prefectural Shrine|Ken-sha]] (as of May 15, Meiji 6) | Established = {{ill|Hosokawa Tadaoki|ja|細川忠興|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, [[Genna (era)|Genna]] 3 (1617) | Main Hall = Nagare-zukuri | Festival = [[Kokura Gion Daiko]] (third Saturday/Sunday in July) }}
'''Yasaka Shrine''' (八坂神社・八阪神社, やさかじんじゃ) refers to {{ill|Shinto shrines|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} named "Yasaka." It is sometimes written as {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|弥栄神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, which is covered in another article.
These shrines are dedicated to {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the deity of {{ill|Gion faith|ja|祇園信仰|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Before the {{ill|Shinto-Buddhism Separation Order|ja|神仏分離令|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Susanoo-no-Mikoto was identified with {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō|1=Gozu Tennō|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.
Other names based on Gion faith include {{ill|Gion Shrine|ja|祇園神社|lt=Gion Shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Hiromine Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|広峯神社 (曖昧さ回避)|lt=Hiromine Shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Tennō Shrine|ja|天王神社|lt=Tennō Shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Tsushima Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|津島神社|lt=Tsushima Shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲神社|lt=Yakumo Shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|八重垣神社|lt=Yaegaki Shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Suga Shrine|ja|須賀神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Susanoo Shrine|ja|素盞嗚神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Susa Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|須佐神社|Susa Shrine (disambiguation)=Susa Shrine (disambiguation)|lt=Susa Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and {{ill|Hikawa Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|氷川神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.
Notably, some exceptions include Yasaka shrines that enshrine {{ill|Yasakatome-no-Kami|ja|八坂刀売神|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.
== Main Shrine == [[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|thumb|250px|right|Kyoto's {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|八坂神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, one of the head shrines]] * '''{{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|八坂神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''' ({{ill|Higashiyama Ward, Kyoto|ja|京都市東山区|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) – Formerly {{ill|Kanjin'in Gion-sha|ja|感神院祇園社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} under {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Mount Hiei|ja|比叡山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} until the Shinto-Buddhism Separation Order. Claimed as the main shrine of Susanoo-no-Mikoto nationwide.
* ''' {{ill|Eki Shrine|ja|疫神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''' – Enshrines {{ill|Somin Shōrai|ja|蘇民将来命|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. '''Yasaka Shrine''' or '''Yasaka Jinja''' (八坂神社・八阪神社, Yasaka Jinja) refers to Shinto shrines that include "Yasaka" in their name. Some may also be written as {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|弥栄神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.
These shrines are part of {{ill|Gion Faith|ja|祇園信仰|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, venerating {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (formerly identified with {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō|1=Gozu Tennō|qq=draft|qq=draft}} before the {{ill|Shinbutsu Bunri|ja|神仏分離|qq=draft|qq=draft}} decree).
Other shrines based on Gion Faith include {{ill|Gion Shrine|ja|祇園神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Hiromine Shrine|ja|広峯神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Tennō Shrine|ja|天王神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Tsushima Shrine|ja|津島神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}<ref>{{ill|Tsushima Faith|ja|津島信仰|qq=draft|qq=draft}}</ref>, {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine|ja|八重垣神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Suga Shrine|ja|須賀神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Susanoo Shrine|ja|素盞嗚神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Susa Shrine|ja|須佐神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and {{ill|Hikawa Shrine|ja|氷川神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}<ref>{{ill|Hikawa Faith|ja|氷川信仰|qq=draft|qq=draft}}</ref>, among others. Their usage varies by historical period and records.
However, there are exceptions where Yasaka Shrines enshrine {{ill|Yasakatome-no-Kami|ja|八坂刀売神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} instead.
The {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kyoto)|ja|八坂神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Higashiyama, Kyoto, claims to be the head shrine of all shrines dedicated to Susanoo-no-Mikoto. Before the Shinbutsu Bunri decree, it was known as {{ill|Kanjin-in Gion-sha|ja|感神院祇園社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} of the {{ill|Tendai sect|ja|天台宗|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, affiliated with {{ill|Mount Hiei|ja|比叡山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.

{{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|250px|right]] | name = Yasaka Shrine (八坂神社) | location = [[Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka]], [[Kitakyushu]], [[Kokurakita Ward]], {{ill|Jōnai|ja|城内 (北九州市)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} | coordinates = {{Coord|33|53|07.68|N|130|52|25.39|E|region:JP-40_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Yasaka Shrine}} | Deities = {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (formerly {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō|1=Gozu Tennō|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) | type = [[Prefectural Shrine|Ken-sha]] (as of May 15, Meiji 6) | Established = {{ill|Hosokawa Tadaoki|ja|細川忠興|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, [[Genna (era)|Genna]] 3 (1617) | Main Hall = Nagare-zukuri | Festival = [[Kokura Gion Daiko]] (third Saturday/Sunday in July) }}
'''Yasaka Shrine''' (八坂神社・八阪神社, やさかじんじゃ) refers to {{ill|Shinto shrines|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} named "Yasaka." It is sometimes written as {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|弥栄神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, which is covered in another article.
These shrines are dedicated to {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the deity of {{ill|Gion faith|ja|祇園信仰|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Before the {{ill|Shinto-Buddhism Separation Order|ja|神仏分離令|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Susanoo-no-Mikoto was identified with {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō|1=Gozu Tennō|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.
Other names based on Gion faith include {{ill|Gion Shrine|ja|祇園神社|lt=Gion Shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Hiromine Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|広峯神社 (曖昧さ回避)|lt=Hiromine Shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Tennō Shrine|ja|天王神社|lt=Tennō Shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Tsushima Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|津島神社|lt=Tsushima Shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲神社|lt=Yakumo Shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|八重垣神社|lt=Yaegaki Shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Suga Shrine|ja|須賀神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Susanoo Shrine|ja|素盞嗚神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Susa Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|須佐神社|Susa Shrine (disambiguation)=Susa Shrine (disambiguation)|lt=Susa Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and {{ill|Hikawa Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|氷川神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.
Notably, some exceptions include Yasaka shrines that enshrine {{ill|Yasakatome-no-Kami|ja|八坂刀売神|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.
== Main Shrine == [[File:Yasaka Jinja.jpg|thumb|250px|right|Kyoto's {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|八坂神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, one of the head shrines]] * '''{{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|八坂神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''' ({{ill|Higashiyama Ward, Kyoto|ja|京都市東山区|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) – Formerly {{ill|Kanjin'in Gion-sha|ja|感神院祇園社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} under {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Mount Hiei|ja|比叡山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} until the Shinto-Buddhism Separation Order. Claimed as the main shrine of Susanoo-no-Mikoto nationwide.
* ''' {{ill|Eki Shrine|ja|疫神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''' – Enshrines {{ill|Somin Shōrai|ja|蘇民将来命|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. '''Yasaka Shrine''' or '''Yasaka Jinja''' (八坂神社・八阪神社, Yasaka Jinja) refers to Shinto shrines that include "Yasaka" in their name. Some may also be written as {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|ja|弥栄神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.
These shrines are part of {{ill|Gion Faith|ja|祇園信仰|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, venerating {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (formerly identified with {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|1=Gozu Tennō|1=Gozu Tennō|qq=draft|qq=draft}} before the {{ill|Shinbutsu Bunri|ja|神仏分離|qq=draft|qq=draft}} decree).
Other shrines based on Gion Faith include {{ill|Gion Shrine|ja|祇園神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Hiromine Shrine|ja|広峯神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Tennō Shrine|ja|天王神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Tsushima Shrine|ja|津島神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}<ref>{{ill|Tsushima Faith|ja|津島信仰|qq=draft|qq=draft}}</ref>, {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine|ja|八重垣神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Suga Shrine|ja|須賀神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Susanoo Shrine|ja|素盞嗚神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Susa Shrine|ja|須佐神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and {{ill|Hikawa Shrine|ja|氷川神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}<ref>{{ill|Hikawa Faith|ja|氷川信仰|qq=draft|qq=draft}}</ref>, among others. Their usage varies by historical period and records.
However, there are exceptions where Yasaka Shrines enshrine {{ill|Yasakatome-no-Kami|ja|八坂刀売神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} instead.
The {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Kyoto)|ja|八坂神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Higashiyama, Kyoto, claims to be the head shrine of all shrines dedicated to Susanoo-no-Mikoto. Before the Shinbutsu Bunri decree, it was known as {{ill|Kanjin-in Gion-sha|ja|感神院祇園社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} of the {{ill|Tendai sect|ja|天台宗|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, affiliated with {{ill|Mount Hiei|ja|比叡山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.
